Enterprise Software Stocks Fall as AI Financing Worries Spread: Palantir and ServiceNow Drop 5%, Salesforce Slides 4%
Palantir, ServiceNow, and Salesforce are sliding hard as investors turn skeptical about who actually pays for the AI buildout powering their growth, and the answer could reshape how the entire software sector gets valued.
Published October 16, 2026, 11:57am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
A digital stock chart displays a mix of green uptrends and red downtrends, reflecting the fluctuating nature of financial markets and individual stock performance. © Thinkstock
Enterprise software is taking the brunt of a fresh pullback in AI-linked stocks, and some of the sector’s biggest names are leading the way lower. Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR | PLTR Price Prediction) shares have slipped 5%, recently changing hands at $190.28.
Meanwhile, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) stock is down 5% to $141.68, in line with the slide in Palantir shares. Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) stock is down 4% to $238.06, marking a slightly smaller decline than Palantir stock and ServiceNow stock are posting.
The selling is notable within the software group. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is down 4%, landing in the same range as Palantir stock, ServiceNow stock and Salesforce stock. Meanwhile, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.35%, representing a softer pullback for large-cap tech.
This decline extends a rotation out of AI-linked stocks as investors question how AI infrastructure spending gets financed. Palantir, ServiceNow and Salesforce all sell software that benefits from that spending, so doubts about its funding feed directly into the pricing of Palantir stock, ServiceNow stock and Salesforce stock.
ServiceNow added a company-specific development on Wednesday, stating that it has no interest or intention of purchasing Decagon, a maker of AI customer-service agents, and that it prioritizes organic growth. Management’s stance keeps ServiceNow focused on building out its own AI agent products in-house. Decagon is privately held, so ServiceNow’s statement doesn’t point to any other listed company.
Palantir sells data analytics and AI software to government and commercial clients through Gotham, Foundry and its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP). Gotham serves government customers, Foundry targets commercial users, and AIP helps organizations put AI to work inside their operations. Its pitch centers on AI sovereignty, the idea that customers can deploy AI while keeping full control of their data.
ServiceNow sells workflow software and Salesforce sells customer-relationship software, both on recurring subscriptions with their own AI agent products. On the product side, ServiceNow’s AI Control Tower governs and deploys enterprise AI agents, while Salesforce builds its pitch around Agentforce. Those subscription models give ServiceNow and Salesforce steadier revenue, yet ServiceNow stock and Salesforce stock are sliding with the rest of the AI-linked group.
Palantir’s bullish thesis rests on its government and commercial AI demand. Palantir serves U.S. defense, intelligence and civilian agencies, international governments and a rapidly expanding base of U.S. commercial enterprises. That diversity gives Palantir more than one source of AI spending to draw from as customers build out their own systems.
The skeptics could read the selloff differently. In the bear case, software tied to AI spending is being marked down with the rest of the AI trade, and Palantir stock has little cushion when sentiment turns. Despite strong customer demand, Palantir shares are falling alongside ServiceNow stock and Salesforce stock.
AI Financing Fears Test Software Premiums
Investors should watch to see if the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF narrows its gap with the Invesco QQQ Trust, which could signal that the software rotation is easing. Palantir’s government and commercial AI demand gives the company a fundamental anchor while that rotation plays out.
The open variable for Palantir, ServiceNow and Salesforce is the depth of the rotation out of AI-linked stocks, with ServiceNow also committed to organic growth after its Decagon statement. A conservative approach fits a selloff driven by financing concerns across the AI trade, so owners of Palantir stock, ServiceNow stock and Salesforce stock should keep their position sizes moderate.

An engineer utilizes sophisticated design software, similar to platforms offered by Cadence Design Systems, to develop complex chips essential for advancing AI technologies. This detailed work is crucial for the AI buildout discussed in the article. © gorodenkoff / iStock via Getty Images
A flat denial of takeover talk is lifting one of the biggest names in enterprise software. ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW | NOW Price Prediction) stock is up 5% to $146.93 in midday trading after the company rejected reports that it planned to buy Decagon, a privately held maker of artificial intelligence (AI) customer-service agents.
Meanwhile, Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) stock is up 4% to $245.39, a gain just shy of the advance in ServiceNow stock. ServiceNow moved to shut down the speculation on October 14. Amit Zavery, the company’s president, chief product officer and chief operating officer, stated, “We are aware of misinformation in the market today about our acquisition strategy. To be clear, ServiceNow has no interest or intention of purchasing Decagon.” Zavery added that the approach to acquisitions is unchanged and that ServiceNow prioritizes organic growth.
Management also sees no major strategic gaps requiring large-scale deals at this time, according to Zavery. Because ServiceNow sells workflow software on recurring subscriptions, the denial of a big acquisition signals where ServiceNow’s margins and product roadmap could be heading, and organic growth tends to keep spending tied to products ServiceNow controls end to end.
Home-grown agent tools already sit inside the ServiceNow lineup, including AI Control Tower for governing enterprise agents, Now Assist and Build Agent. That catalog gives ServiceNow an internal path into customer-service automation, the niche where Decagon competes.
Sector funds are splitting along the same line as ServiceNow stock and Palantir stock. For a sector read, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is up 0.9% to $108.65, a far smaller gain than the move in ServiceNow stock. Across large-cap technology, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.7% to $723.84, sliding in the same direction as Palantir stock.
Holders of both the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust are seeing their portfolios pulled in opposite directions. Because Palantir is a component of the Invesco QQQ Trust, the dip in Palantir stock and the fund’s decline land on the same side of the ledger.
On the bullish side, ServiceNow’s subscription model and its stated focus on organic growth could protect the margins that steady revenue supports, and skipping a large deal keeps management’s attention on shipping its own agent products. Recurring contracts give ServiceNow a predictable base that a big acquisition might have complicated.
However, a denial removes a rumor without adding new revenue for ServiceNow, and headline-driven gains can fade once the news moves on. Startups building AI customer-service agents, Decagon among them, show how crowded the ServiceNow corner of the market is becoming.
Salesforce offers a parallel story. Bulls see its Agentforce platform as proof that organic agent products can win customers, though bears may note today’s gain rests on sympathy rather than company-specific news. Palantir differs from both. Bulls point to its data-analytics strength with government and commercial clients, while bears argue its far higher valuation leaves room for more profit-taking on crowded agentic AI headlines (we profiled seven companies driving the AI expansion beyond the chipmakers in a free report here).
ServiceNow currently faces the question of whether organic product releases carry the roadmap the company says it doesn’t need deals to fill. Zavery’s comments set that bar publicly, which gives each product launch more weight in the debate over ServiceNow stock. Customer adoption of the existing agent lineup may offer the clearest early evidence.
Salesforce and Palantir face tests of their own. Salesforce must show its agent products keep drawing customers once the sympathy rally cools off, while Palantir must defend its premium as rivals crowd the agentic AI field. The takeaway: investors should keep their positions in ServiceNow stock moderate until adoption evidence arrives, and watch for whether gains broaden across the software group.

Workflow software spreads sideways. A company buys it for one department, the next department wants the same thing, and the cost of adding them is small because the platform is already there.

Palo Alto Networks sells security software to large companies, and by most measures it is doing well. Revenue rose 34.50% in its most recent quarter, and the shares have doubled in six months. The reported profit does not look like any of that. The company earned $307 million on revenue of $11.48 billion, and much of the explanation sits in how it pays its staff.

Why the Cash Looks Nothing Like the Profit:
Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.
Strip it out and the business looks entirely different. Operating cash flow reached $4.55 billion across the same year, more than fourteen times the reported profit, and borrowing is negligible at 9.34% of equity.

Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.

The stock changes hands at 94.34 times what analysts expect next year. That multiple is built on earnings measured after adding the share-based cost back, not on the profit the company actually reported.
So the price depends on which definition a buyer accepts. On the reported figure, the stock is extraordinarily expensive, and on the adjusted one it is merely expensive. Security budgets have been growing quickly. 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy in 2026 has the names competing for them.
Conclusion:
This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. That cost falls on owners through dilution rather than on the company through cash, and the tax line closed what was left. Watch the share count rather than the earnings line, because that is where this particular cost is actually recorded.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of remote code execution in the management interface.
"A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall," Palo Alto Networks said.
The issue impacts PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series). Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected by the vulnerability.
Palo Alto Networks said that no special configuration is required to exploit the issue, but said the security risk can be minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses.
"You can reduce the risk of exploitation by restricting access to a jump box that is the only system allowed to access the management interface," it said.

Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices.
Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks.
"Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said.
The vulnerability has a severity score of 8.6 and affects PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, as well as Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances. Palo Alto says Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.
To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface.
Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only.
The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.
Customers running older, unsupported versions must upgrade to a supported release.
Palo Alto says there are no known workarounds for the vulnerability, but customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can enable signatures that provide limited protection against known attack patterns.
"Limited coverage in Threat Prevention means that while known attack patterns can be identified using the current Threat ID, variations may exist that cannot currently be detected," warns Palo Alto.
"If this CVE and Required Configuration for Exposure impact your environment, we recommend upgrading to an unaffected version."
The vulnerability was discovered internally by Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks.
The company also shared three IP addresses that have been exploiting the flaw: 66.42.72[.]14, 208.83.239[.]114, and 149.248.47[.]234.
BleepingComputer contacted Palo Alto Networks to learn when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks, and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to access internal networks.
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has now added CVE-2026-0322 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requires federal civilian agencies to mitigate the vulnerability by October 17.

Palo Alto (PANW) Pays a Large Part of Its Wage Bill in Stock. What Does That Do to Profit?
Why the Cash Looks Nothing Like the Profit:
Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.
Strip it out and the business looks entirely different. Operating cash flow reached $4.55 billion across the same year, more than fourteen times the reported profit, and borrowing is negligible at 9.34% of equity.

Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.

Which Number the Price Is Using:
The stock changes hands at 94.34 times what analysts expect next year. That multiple is built on earnings measured after adding the share-based cost back, not on the profit the company actually reported.
So the price depends on which definition a buyer accepts. On the reported figure, the stock is extraordinarily expensive, and on the adjusted one it is merely expensive. Security budgets have been growing quickly. 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy in 2026 has the names competing for them.
Conclusion:
This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. That cost falls on owners through dilution rather than on the company through cash, and the tax line closed what was left. Watch the share count rather than the earnings line, because that is where this particular cost is actually recorded.

Why the Cash Looks Nothing Like the Profit:
Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.
Strip it out and the business looks entirely different. Operating cash flow reached $4.55 billion across the same year, more than fourteen times the reported profit, and borrowing is negligible at 9.34% of equity.
Palo Alto is one of the ten in our 10 Most Promising Cloud Stocks According to Hedge Funds. To see which companies rank above it, click HERE.
Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.

Which Number the Price Is Using:
The stock changes hands at 94.34 times what analysts expect next year. That multiple is built on earnings measured after adding the share-based cost back, not on the profit the company actually reported.
So the price depends on which definition a buyer accepts. On the reported figure, the stock is extraordinarily expensive, and on the adjusted one it is merely expensive. Security budgets have been growing quickly. 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy in 2026 has the names competing for them.
Conclusion:
This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. That cost falls on owners through dilution rather than on the company through cash, and the tax line closed what was left. Watch the share count rather than the earnings line, because that is where this particular cost is actually recorded.

Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation
Ravie LakshmananOct 15, 2026Vulnerability / Network Security
Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday issued security updates for a high-severity flaw in PAN-OS software that has come under active exploitation.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of remote code execution in the management interface.
"A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall," Palo Alto Networks said.
The issue impacts PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series). Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected by the vulnerability.
Palo Alto Networks said that no special configuration is required to exploit the issue, but said the security risk can be minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses.
"You can reduce the risk of exploitation by restricting access to a jump box that is the only system allowed to access the management interface," it said.
Patches are available in the following versions -
PAN-OS >= 12.1.4-h12, >= 12.1.7-h8, >= 12.1.10-h2
PAN-OS >= 11.2.4-h22, >= 11.2.7-h21, >= 11.2.10-h15, >= 11.2.13-h3, >= 11.2.16 (ETA: October 15, 2026)
PAN-OS >= 11.1.4-h37, >= 11.1.6-h39, >= 11.1.7-h11, >= 11.1.10-h35, >= 11.1.13-h15, >= 11.1.16-h3
PAN-OS >= 10.2.7-h38, >= 10.2.10-h41, >= 10.2.13-h26, >= 10.2.16-h11, >= 10.2.18-h12
The network security company also acknowledged it has seen "very limited exploitation" targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface, but did not elaborate on the nature of the malicious activity involved, who is behind the effort, or when it began.
The following IP addresses geolocated to the U.S. are assessed to be linked to the exploit attempts -
It credited Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks, with discovering and reporting the vulnerability.
The disclosure comes as Cisco warned that threat actors are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76519, CVSS score: 9.8) that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.
"This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled," it said. "An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system."
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has since added both CVE-2026-0322 and CVE-2026-76519 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to prioritize fixes by October 17, 2026.

Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
The vulnerability affects the PAN-OS management interface and lets authenticated attackers with network access execute code as root on vulnerable devices.
Palo Alto Networks confirmed in a security advisory published Wednesday that it has seen limited exploitation of the flaw in attacks.
"Very limited exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface," the company said.
The vulnerability has a severity score of 8.6 and affects PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, as well as Panorama virtual and M-Series appliances. Palo Alto says Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected.
To exploit the vulnerability, attackers need existing credentials and network access to the PAN-OS management interface.
Therefore, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to the management interface to trusted internal IP addresses only.
The company has released fixes for affected PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 versions, with a fix for PAN-OS 11.2.16 expected on October 15.
Customers running older, unsupported versions must upgrade to a supported release.
Palo Alto says there are no known workarounds for the vulnerability, but customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can enable signatures that provide limited protection against known attack patterns.
"Limited coverage in Threat Prevention means that while known attack patterns can be identified using the current Threat ID, variations may exist that cannot currently be detected," warns Palo Alto.
"If this CVE and Required Configuration for Exposure impact your environment, we recommend upgrading to an unaffected version."
The vulnerability was discovered internally by Suraj Siddharudh, a senior principal product security researcher at Palo Alto Networks.
The company also shared three IP addresses that have been exploiting the flaw: 66.42.72[.]14, 208.83.239[.]114, and 149.248.47[.]234.
BleepingComputer contacted Palo Alto Networks to learn when exploitation began, who is behind the attacks, and whether attackers compromised firewalls or used them to access internal networks.
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has now added CVE-2026-0322 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requires federal civilian agencies to mitigate the vulnerability by October 17.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) Pays a Large Part of Its Wage Bill in Stock. What Does That Do to Profit?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:49 AM CDT 4 min read
Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW) closed at $346.95 on October 19. The stock has returned 104.62% over the last 6 months, compared to an 11.6% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 8.7% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.
Palo Alto Networks sells security software to large companies, and by most measures it is doing well. Revenue rose 34.50% in its most recent quarter, and the shares have doubled in six months. The reported profit does not look like any of that. The company earned $307 million on revenue of $11.48 billion, and much of the explanation sits in how it pays its staff.
READ ALSO: 10 Most Profitable Undervalued Stocks to Invest In
Palo Alto (PANW) Pays a Large Part of Its Wage Bill in Stock. What Does That Do to Profit?
Why the Cash Looks Nothing Like the Profit:
Share-based compensation and related charges came to $1.71 billion in the last financial year, more than twice what the business made at the operating line. That is issued in stock rather than paid out, so it never leaves as cash.
Strip it out and the business looks entirely different. Operating cash flow reached $4.55 billion across the same year, more than fourteen times the reported profit, and borrowing is negligible at 9.34% of equity.
Palo Alto is one of the ten in our 10 Most Promising Cloud Stocks According to Hedge Funds. To see which companies rank above it, click HERE.
Why It Is Still a Cost:
Paying in shares is not free simply because no cash moves. Every share issued to an employee makes each existing share a smaller claim on the company, so the cost lands on the owners rather than on the business.
The scale of it is what makes this one unusual. The charge dwarfs the profit the company reported, which means the owners are funding some of those wages out of their own stake.
Share-based pay is not the full explanation. A swing in other income and a heavier tax charge covered the rest of the distance to the bottom line. So the charge explains the shape of this profit rather than all of its direction.
DON'T MISS: 10 Best Fundamental Stocks to Invest in According to Billionaires
Which Number the Price Is Using:
The stock changes hands at 94.34 times what analysts expect next year. That multiple is built on earnings measured after adding the share-based cost back, not on the profit the company actually reported.
So the price depends on which definition a buyer accepts. On the reported figure, the stock is extraordinarily expensive, and on the adjusted one it is merely expensive. Security budgets have been growing quickly. 10 Best Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy in 2026 has the names competing for them.
Conclusion:
This is a good business that reports two very different pictures of itself, and both are accurate. The cash generation is real, the borrowing is light, and the growth is quick for a business of this size. What holds the headline profit down is largely the cost of settling a big share of the wage bill in stock. That cost falls on owners through dilution rather than on the company through cash, and the tax line closed what was left. Watch the share count rather than the earnings line, because that is where this particular cost is actually recorded.

Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW) was held by 89 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $5.49 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is up from 87 hedge fund holders in the previous quarter.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 1, 2026 — Palo Alto Networks® (NASDAQ: PANW), the global AI cybersecurity leader, announced today financial results for its fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal year, ended July 31, 2026.
"We delivered a strong Q4 to close out the year, adding nearly $1 billion of Net New NGS ARR in a single quarter," said Nikesh Arora, chairman and chief executive officer of Palo Alto Networks. "The latest advancements in AI are elevating cybersecurity to the top of the CIO priority list, and will serve as durable tailwinds as we progress towards our $20 billion FY30 NGS ARR target."
"We delivered a strong finish to a record year and exceeded our guidance across the board, fueled by strength across our Network & AI Security, Cortex, and Idira platforms," said Dipak Golechha, chief financial officer of Palo Alto Networks. "Our profitable growth framework continues to scale effectively, reinforcing our confidence in achieving 40% adjusted free cash flow margin in FY28."
Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Highlights
•Total revenue for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 grew 34% year over year to $3.41 billion.
•Next-Generation Security ARR for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 grew 63% year over year to $9.10 billion.
•Remaining performance obligations grew 34% year over year to $21.2 billion.
•GAAP operating income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $172 million, compared with GAAP operating income of $497 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Non-GAAP operating income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.0 billion, compared with non-GAAP operating income of $768 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
•GAAP net loss for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $282 million, or ($0.35) per diluted share, compared with GAAP net income of $254 million, or $0.36 per diluted share, for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Non-GAAP net income for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $853 million, or $1.02 per diluted share, compared with non-GAAP net income of $673 million, or $0.95 per diluted share, for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
•Net cash provided by operating activities for the fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.4 billion, compared with net cash provided by operating activities of $1.0 billion for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Adjusted free cash flow for fiscal fourth quarter 2026 was $1.3 billion, compared with adjusted free cash flow of $954 million for the fiscal fourth quarter 2025. Fiscal year 2026 adjusted free cash flow margin was 38.4%. A reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP information is contained in the tables below.
Palo Alto Networks has acquired Console, an AI-native platform that enables agentic workflows across enterprise operations. Console will expand the role of our Cortex platform across the broader enterprise agentic transformation.
Palo Alto Networks provides guidance based on current market conditions and expectations.
For the fiscal first quarter 2027, we expect:
•Next-Generation Security ARR of $9.54 billion to $9.56 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 63%.
•Remaining performance obligations of $20.8 billion to $20.9 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 34% to 35%.
•Total revenue in the range of $3.300 billion to $3.310 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 33% to 34%.
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $0.96 to $0.98, using 837 million to 844 million shares outstanding.
For the fiscal year 2027, we expect:
•Next-Generation Security ARR of $11.075 billion to $11.175 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 22% to 23%.
•Remaining performance obligations of $25.2 billion to $25.4 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 19% to 20%.
•Total revenue in the range of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 23% to 24%.
•Non-GAAP operating margin of 29.5%.
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $4.16 to $4.19, using 844 million to 847 million shares outstanding.
•Adjusted free cash flow margin to be 38.0%.
Guidance for non-GAAP financial measures excludes share-based compensation-related charges, including share-based payroll tax expense, acquisition-related costs, including change in fair value of contingent consideration liability, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, litigation-related charges, non-cash charges related to convertible notes, change in fair value of convertible senior notes and capped calls, and income tax and other tax adjustments related to our long-term non-GAAP effective tax rate, along with certain non-recurring expenses and certain non-recurring cash flows. We have not reconciled non-GAAP operating margin guidance to GAAP operating margin, diluted non-GAAP net income per share guidance to GAAP net income (loss) per diluted share, or adjusted free cash flow margin guidance to GAAP net cash provided by operating activities because we do not provide guidance on GAAP operating margin, GAAP net income (loss) or net cash provided by operating activities and would not be able to present the various reconciling cash and non-cash items between GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures because certain items that impact these measures are uncertain or out of our control, or cannot be reasonably predicted, including share-based compensation expense, without unreasonable effort. The actual amounts of such reconciling items will have a significant impact on the company’s GAAP net income (loss) per diluted share, GAAP operating margin and GAAP net cash provided by operating activities.
Palo Alto Networks will host a video webcast for analysts and investors to discuss the company’s fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026 results as well as the outlook for its fiscal first quarter and fiscal year 2027 today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time/1:30 p.m. Pacific time. Open to the public, investors may access the webcast, supplemental financial information and earnings slides from the "Investors" section of the company’s website at investors.paloaltonetworks.com. A replay will be available three hours after the conclusion of the webcast and archived for one year.
This press release contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions including statements regarding our financial and operating results and financial outlook for the fiscal first quarter 2027 and fiscal year 2027. There are a significant number of factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements made or implied in this press release, including: unfavorable economic and market conditions and the uncertain geopolitical environment; our ability to effectively manage future growth and improve our systems, processes, and controls; our ability to maintain our revenue growth rate or profitability; variability and seasonality in our operating results; our ability to sell new and additional products, subscriptions, and support offerings to existing and new customers; the delayed recognition of revenue from subscription and support offerings; revenue volatility from consumption- or usage-based offerings and customer usage optimization behavior; potential decreases in the sales prices of our products, subscriptions, and support offerings; our reliance on channel partners; credit and liquidity risk exposure; challenges associated with sales to government entities; intense competition in our markets; risks associated with the evolving definition of the identity security market; customer trends toward vendor consolidation in cybersecurity; competition from cloud infrastructure providers offering native security capabilities; risks related to past and future acquisitions; our ability to predict, prepare for, and respond to rapidly evolving technological and
market developments; the need to maintain a broad ecosystem of third-party technology integrations; risks related to the development, deployment, or use of AI, including AI agents as a new class of identity; the impact of network or data security incidents; defects, errors, or vulnerabilities in our products and subscriptions; reliance on customers to configure and use our products securely; the quality of our technical support services; our ability to meet service-level commitments; our reliance on data center facilities operated by third-party cloud service providers; intellectual property claims and our ability to protect proprietary rights; risks associated with open source software; our reliance on third-party technology licenses; dependence on manufacturing partners and limited sources of supply; our ability to attract, retain, and motivate key personnel; risks associated with international sales and operations, including export and import controls; fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates; risks associated with operations and employees located in Israel; costs and risks related to compliance with privacy and data protection laws; potential tax liabilities; risks related to estimates, judgments, and critical accounting policies; our ability to maintain proper and effective internal control over financial reporting; risks related to corporate responsibility matters; dilution from issuance of additional common stock; risks related to our convertible senior notes, including our ability to settle conversions, repurchase, or repay such notes and the potential effect of capped call transactions.
Additional risks and uncertainties on these and other factors that could affect our financial results and cause actual results to differ materially from those described in the forward-looking statements we make in this press release are included under the captions "Risk Factors" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our annual reports on Form 10-K and quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, which are available on our website at investors.paloaltonetworks.com and on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov. Additional information and risks and uncertainties will also be set forth in other documents that we file with or furnish to the SEC from time to time. All forward-looking statements in this press release are based on our current beliefs and information available to management as of the date hereof and are inherently uncertain, and we do not assume any obligation to update the forward-looking statements provided to reflect events that occur or circumstances that exist after the date on which they were made, except as required by law.
Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Key Metrics
Palo Alto Networks has provided in this press release financial information that has not been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (GAAP). The company uses these non-GAAP financial measures and other key metrics internally in analyzing its financial results and believes that the use of these non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics are helpful to investors as an additional tool to evaluate ongoing operating results and trends, and in comparing the company’s financial results with other companies in its industry, many of which present similar non-GAAP financial measures or key metrics.
The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures and key metrics are not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for comparable GAAP financial measures and should be read only in conjunction with the company’s consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of the company’s historical non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release, and investors are encouraged to review these reconciliations.
Non-GAAP operating income. Palo Alto Networks defines non-GAAP operating income as operating income plus share-based compensation-related charges, including share-based payroll tax expense, acquisition-related costs, including change in fair value of contingent consideration liability, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, and litigation-related charges. The company believes that non-GAAP operating income provides management and investors with greater visibility into the underlying performance of the company’s core business operating results.
Non-GAAP net income and net income per share, diluted. Palo Alto Networks defines non-GAAP net income as net income (loss) plus share-based compensation-related charges, including share-based payroll tax expense, acquisition-related costs, including change in fair value of contingent consideration liability, amortization expense of acquired intangible assets, litigation-related charges, non-cash charges related to convertible notes, and change in fair value of convertible senior notes and capped calls. The company also excludes from non-GAAP income tax and other tax adjustments related to our long-term non-GAAP effective tax rate in order to provide a complete picture of the company’s recurring core business operating results. The company defines non-GAAP net income per share, diluted, as non-GAAP net income divided by the weighted-average diluted shares outstanding, which includes the potentially dilutive effect of the company’s employee equity incentive plan awards and the company’s convertible senior notes and related warrants, after giving effect to the anti-dilutive impact of the company’s note hedge agreements and capped call transactions, which reduced the potential economic dilution that otherwise would have occurred in connection with the conversion and settlement of the company’s convertible senior notes. Under GAAP, the anti-dilutive impact of the note hedge or capped calls is not reflected in diluted shares outstanding. The company considers these non-GAAP financial measures to be useful metrics for management and investors for the same reasons that it uses non-GAAP operating income.
Adjusted free cash flow margin, adjusted free cash flow, and free cash flow. Palo Alto Networks defines adjusted free cash flow margin, a non-GAAP measure, as adjusted free cash flow divided by total revenue. The company defines adjusted free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, as free cash flow, plus certain capital expenditures for our headquarters and certain corporate assets, plus payments of acquisition-related costs, plus litigation-related payments. The company defines free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, as net cash provided by operating activities less purchases of property, equipment, and other assets. We consider free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow margin to be operating metrics as well as liquidity measures that provide useful information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated by the business after necessary capital expenditures and before the impact of certain qualifying non-recurring cash payments from operating activities, as applicable. A limitation of the utility of free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow as a measure of our liquidity is that it does not represent the total increase or decrease in our cash balance for the period. In addition, it is important to note that other companies, including companies in our industry, may not use free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow, may calculate free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow in a different manner than we do, or may use other financial measures to evaluate their liquidity, all of which could reduce the usefulness of free cash flow or adjusted free cash flow as a comparative measure.

Cisco Announces Webex AI Agents for Meetings and Customer Service
Cisco announces Webex AI agents for meetings and customer service. Learn what IT teams should check about availability, integrations and access controls.
Cisco announced new Webex AI agent capabilities at WebexOne 2026, outlining plans for collaboration and customer-service workflows. Image: Cisco
Cisco wants AI agents to work inside Webex meetings, messages and customer-service workflows, giving IT teams new integration and oversight decisions.
Cisco announced new agentic capabilities at WebexOne on Oct. 7, designed to help AI agents use shared context and carry out multi-step tasks across collaboration and customer-service systems.
The announcements include Dialog for maintaining customer context across interactions and planned capabilities for agents to participate in Webex spaces, meetings and calls. Several features remain forthcoming
Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer at Cisco says that “the next era of work isn’t about bolting chatbots onto yesterday’s tools,” but rather “about AI agents working alongside people and teams.”
Cisco’s Webex is bringing together enterprise context, collaboration software and AI agents to its platform. The company is extending this idea beyond video conferencing into workplace management and customer service.
Cisco describes workflows in which employees could @mention an analytics agent in a Webex space to retrieve usage statistics, then ask a presentation agent to update a PowerPoint deck.
For customer service, Cisco introduced Dialog, a software layer connecting enterprise systems with the Webex AI Agent platform. Cisco says it is designed to maintain customer context across interactions and coordinate follow-up work after a conversation ends.
Cisco anticipates beta availability in the first quarter of calendar 2027, with release timing subject to change

AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

The Ultra-Dense Small Form-Factor Pluggable (USFP) is industry’s first pluggable form factor designed to help customers scale AI networks, providing a path to up to 12.8T of aggregate capacity while preserving proven deployment and serviceability models
As AI evolves from answering prompts to orchestrating complex, multi-step workflows, infrastructure demands are growing rapidly. From training and inference to emerging agentic AI systems, modern AI workloads depend on continuous communication across accelerators, applications, storage, and services, driving unprecedented requirements for bandwidth, responsiveness, and scale.
At Cisco, we believe the future of AI networking will be defined by how effectively silicon, systems, optics, software, and operations work together as a full-stack platform, enabling customers to scale AI with greater performance, efficiency, serviceability, and investment protection by optimizing every layer of the infrastructure together. Customers should not have to redesign their infrastructure or abandon established operational models to take advantage of the next generation of networking innovation.
Today, together with NVIDIA, we are announcing design plans for USFP, the industry’s first 400G-per-lane capable pluggable form factor designed to enable the next generation of AI Ethernet fabrics. USFP will provide a path supporting both 200G and 400G SerDes based systems and ASICs , helping customers scale from today’s 1.6T fabrics, with the ability to achieve 12.8T of overall pluggable capacity while preserving the benefits that have made pluggable optics successful.
As AI clusters grow across data centers, clouds, and edge environments, networks must carry significantly more traffic while balancing power, cooling, operational flexibility, and serviceability.
USFP is the next step in that journey. It addresses a critical industry challenge: delivering higher capacity AI fabrics without disrupting the manufacturing, deployment, and operational models that have enabled the scale and success of the pluggable ecosystem.
That perspective has shaped Cisco and NVIDIA’s collaboration for years. Together, we have helped customers build increasingly sophisticated infrastructure spanning networking, security, AI systems, and high-performance AI fabrics. Our work has been guided by a shared goal: helping customers accelerate AI adoption while maintaining flexibility, openness, and choice.
Preserving what works while advancing what’s next
The future of AI networking will not be defined by a single architectural approach. The industry continues to innovate across pluggable, near-packaged, co-packaged, and other emerging optical architectures, each with different advantages and tradeoffs. Customers will choose the technologies that best align with their operational requirements and long-term infrastructure strategies.
Organizations continue to value independently field replaceable modules, mature supply chains, interoperability across suppliers, and familiar serviceability models. These advantages become even more important as AI environments grow in scale and complexity.
USFP will extend those benefits into the next era of AI networking. It will provide a path toward higher capacity AI fabrics and higher density networking switch and compute equipment, while preserving the operational simplicity, openness, and ecosystem flexibility data center operators rely on today.
Accelerating the next generation of AI fabrics
USFP was designed with a simple objective: help AI networks scale efficiently.
With 16 lanes capable of operating at 400 Gb/s per lane, USFP will deliver 6.4T of aggregate capacity, four times the bandwidth density of today’s 1.6T pluggables. The architecture can scale to 32 lanes, providing a path to 12.8T of aggregate capacity. It also creates an opportunity for approximately 1.3x greater power efficiency through the use of 400G SerDes technology, helping operators manage growing power and cooling demands.
Together, these innovations create a foundation for higher-capacity AI Ethernet fabrics and continued innovation across the pluggable networking ecosystem.
To help customers scale AI infrastructure efficiently and sustainably, Cisco takes a full-stack, co-designed platform approach that combines silicon, high-density systems, optics, software, and operational expertise.
USFP reflects that philosophy. Rather than a standalone innovation, it is part of a broader platform vision that advances scale, efficiency, and performance while preserving the deployment, serviceability, and lifecycle models customers depend on.
USFP enables the industry to accelerate AI by building on the ecosystem models that have powered today’s AI networks. By combining a path to higher-capacity fabrics and improved efficiency with familiar operational practices, USFP helps customers scale AI infrastructure while maintaining the flexibility, interoperability, and consistency required at scale.
Cisco has long championed open ecosystems and industry collaboration to accelerate innovation and customer adoption. We see USFP as an extension of that approach, helping create a foundation for broad industry participation, interoperability, and long-term investment protection.
As AI networks continue to grow, Cisco and NVIDIA remain committed to delivering innovations that advance performance while preserving the operational foundations customers trust.

How Much Of Cisco Stock's Rise Did The Business Earn?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:02 AM CDT 4 min read
Cisco Systems (CSCO) supplies businesses and the hyperscalers building AI infrastructure with networking and security products, along with services. The company's stock climbed 92% between late July 2021 and mid-October 2026, before dividends. A rally of that magnitude makes it natural to credit a growing business. So take a guess: how much of that rise came from Cisco selling more?
How Much Did Cisco's Sales Grow?
Cisco expanded its sales 27% over those five years. The company generated $63.3 billion in the twelve months to July 2026, compared with $49.8 billion in the twelve months to July 2021. That growth accounts for a little over a third of the stock's rise. Because the four changes multiply together, each portion of the rise is measured on a scale that lets them add up to 100%.
Expanding the business represents a real achievement. Yet nearly two thirds of the stock's advance came from somewhere else.
What Else Lifted Cisco Stock?
As the table details, most of the remaining gain came from what investors pay for Cisco's profit.
The price-to-earnings multiple, representing what investors pay for each dollar of profit, served as the largest source. Cisco's multiple rose from 22.1 to 32.0, and that expansion provided more than half of the stock's overall gain. The company also kept repurchasing stock, including during its latest quarter. The share count fell 5.8%, which added about a tenth of the rise. Meanwhile, Cisco's net margin, the share of sales the company keeps as profit, slipped slightly and pulled the price down a little.
So investors assigning a higher value to Cisco's profit did more for the stock than business growth did.
Can Margins And Multiples Keep Rising?
Multiples and margins cannot expand indefinitely, whereas sales can increase for as long as Cisco keeps selling more. The company's margin sat at 21.0% over the latest twelve months. That figure stands below the 26% it reached over the twelve months to the third quarter of fiscal 2019, marking its high for the past ten years.
By contrast, the multiple sits higher today than it did at 36 of the 40 quarter ends since fiscal 2017. The lift Cisco received from its multiple is therefore unlikely to repeat the way sales growth can.
What Cisco Would Need To Repeat Its Rise
If the margin, the multiple and the share count remained where they are, Cisco's sales would need to grow about 13.3% a year for the next five and a quarter years to give the stock the same rise. That future timeframe matches the window of the stock's historical rally. Over the past five years, Cisco grew sales 4.9% a year.
Sales are growing faster now. Sales rose 11.8% in fiscal 2026 and 17.6% in the quarter to July 2026. The Networking business led the expansion, growing 22.5% for the year. Management said about 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue came from AI infrastructure for hyperscalers, up from less than 2% in fiscal 2025.
Measured against the pace required for a repeat performance, Cisco's sales growth is the figure to watch in its next report, expected on or around November 10, 2026.

Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO | CSCO Price Prediction | CSCO Price Prediction) sits in the middle of what its CEO calls a networking super cycle. Last quarter, product revenue rose 24% to $13.46B and networking climbed 28% to $9.79B. AI orders reached $9.30B for fiscal 2026.
Shares are up 43.91% YTD, yet they trade at $108.87 after a 4.2% drop today. Chuck Robbins said it directly: “We believe we’re only at the beginning of this super cycle.” So can Cisco reach $200 by 2030?
The stock has lost momentum. Shares fell 7.26% over the past week and 0.71% over the past month. They now trade below the 52-week high of $129.38. Investors are focused on margins.
Non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 66.3% from 68.4% as lower-margin AI hardware took a bigger share of sales. Management also highlighted memory costs and uneven hyperscaler order timing. With a beta of 0.979, Cisco usually tracks the broader market, which makes a sharp one-day drop a clear sign of investor nerves.
Wall Street Sees 25.1% Upside. Our Model Says 19.5%
The consensus target is $136.16, an upside of 25.1%. It rests on 5 Strong Buy, 14 Buy, 10 Hold and 0 Sell ratings. Our one-year base case is $130.14, a 19.5% gain. The scenarios run from $109.27 in the bear case to $138.12 in the bull case, and model confidence is high at 0.9.
In my view, both expectations underestimate Cisco’s earnings. Earnings grew 52.1% year over year, yet only 66% of analysts rate the stock bullish. Ten Holds on a company guiding to $5.05 to $5.11 in fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS strike me as too conservative.
Here’s What It Takes for Cisco to Reach $200
To get to $200 from today’s price of $108.87 would require a gain of 83.7%.
With forward EPS of $5.146, a price of $200 implies a forward P/E of 39x. Our base case of $130.14 already implies 26x, so the bold target requires 13x of additional multiple expansion.
Today’s valuation looks steep, but the math shifts over time. If EPS compounds at the 9.23% consensus growth rate through fiscal 2030, it reaches about $6.71, and $200 works out to roughly 30x.
Earnings growth does most of the lifting. An adjustment factor of 1.125 reflects technology sector momentum and strong earnings acceleration, with the five-year bull case already reaching $187.86.
The catalysts keep coming. Cisco expects AI infrastructure revenue of $7.5B in fiscal 2027, roughly double fiscal 2026. Recent releases highlighted Splunk advancements for trusted AI, new agentic collaboration experiences and scalability and openness at OCP 2026.
Robbins added: “The network remains an absolute critical factor as to whether AI deployments succeed or fail.” Cisco is one of several picks-and-shovels names gaining from the data-center expansion (we rounded up seven of these AI infrastructure suppliers, networking included, in a free report here).
A major risk is that hyperscaler AI spending cools before enterprise demand can fill the gap.
Where Cisco Trades Today vs Its Earnings Power
At $108.87, Cisco trades at 21x forward EPS. That’s a reasonable multiple for a company guiding to $72.2B to $73.4B in fiscal 2027 revenue, up from $63.33B in fiscal 2026.
Shares sit between a 52-week low of $67.32 and a high of $129.38. Over 10 years, the stock has returned 383.19%. A 21x multiple on accelerating earnings leaves room for the bull case to play out.
$200 Is a Stretch, But Here’s Why It’s Possible
Hitting $200 by 2030 would take an 83.7% gain. I see it as a stretch, though a reachable one. Three things need to go right. AI infrastructure revenue has to keep growing past $7.5B. Security growth needs to improve to high single digits, as management expects. Operating margins also have to hold near 35% while gross margin slips.
A sharp pullback in hyperscaler capex would undermine the thesis. Returns at this level shouldn’t be expected every year, but we’ve outlined the path for how Cisco could reach $200 in 2030.

Piper Sandler cuts Cisco price target to $125 on growth peak fears
Cisco stock shed nearly 5% on Tuesday after Piper Sandler analyst James Fish cut the firm's price target on the networking equipment company to $125 from $132, while holding a Neutral rating in place.
Fish and his team pointed to reduced price-to-earnings multiple assumptions, with the analysts expressing concern that the industry's growth trajectory may be approaching its ceiling, according to CNBC. Cisco stock closed Tuesday at $106.44.

Skeptical analysts countered that underlying sales expansion would retreat to single-digit territory. Piper Sandler described the company's own outlook as "conservative" relative to what broader market demand would support, according to CNBC.

Cisco Wants To Be The ‘Switzerland’ Of Enterprise AI
Cisco is betting that an open, vendor-agnostic approach to AI models and agents can differentiate it from rivals while giving partners more ways to win.
While some vendors are increasingly pushing proprietary AI ecosystems, Cisco wants to position itself as the neutral orchestration layer that connects competing AI models and agents.
If Cisco succeeds in its strategy, essentially networking for AI agents, partners won’t have to choose one AI winner, the company believes.
Cisco executives during WebexOne 2026 earlier this month repeatedly emphasized the tech giant’s support for third-party models, bring-your-own-LLM flexibility and agent interoperability and openness. The company is pitching itself as the agnostic layer where enterprises can work with AI regardless of whether the underlying model comes from companies including Google, Anthropic or OpenAI.
That strategy extends to Cisco’s emerging agentic AI vision, according to Snorre Kjesbu, senior vice president and general manager of Cisco Collaboration.
“Cisco is going to be Switzerland when it comes to working with a lot of players,” he said.
Cisco is already there in the collaboration space, pointing to the company’s interoperability with competing vendors. “We’re thinking the same way also on the agent side, but we need to push innovation as well at the same time,” Kjesbu said.
[Related: 8 New Cisco Workplace And AI Innovations Unveiled At WebexOne 2026]
Cisco is backing that strategy with support for third-party AI models and agents inside its Webex platform, including bring-your-own-LLM capabilities, agent-to-agent interoperability and integrations with external AI providers rather than locking customers into a Cisco-only stack.
Cisco’s integration with Claude, OpenAI-related tools, and other assistants is a shift in strategy for the tech giant, according to Joe Berger, vice president of digital experiences for longtime Cisco top partner World Wide Technology, Maryland Heights, Mo.
“They’re not going to win everything, but they can work with most of the vendors to supply components of it. I think it’s the right approach because I don’t think there’s a winner right now that’s been clearly defined,” he said.
Cisco’s willingness to work across competing platforms is a departure from its longtime approach to the market that’s been evident until recently, Berger said.
“If you look back five years ago, that was a hard pill for them to swallow, being agnostic, and now I think they’re winning more collab deals because they are working with Microsoft and Zoom and now Google. I think that’s the approach they have to take with the broader Cisco portfolio,” he said.
Cisco has realized it has to meet the customers where they are, and the customer might be with a competitor, Berger added.
“If they have that customer-first mindset, ideally, it still brings business to Cisco, whether it’s in a day or in two years. I think it sets them up to be well positioned," he said.
Cisco said it doesn’t want to own the underlying AI model and instead believes its opportunity lies in providing the networking, security, observability and management layers that sit on top of multiple AI platforms. It’s an approach that could be a win for partners, which won’t have to bet their business on one AI model and will be able to build services around multiple models, the company believes.
In fact, Cisco could carve out a unique role for itself as a neutral AI platform because the tech giant isn’t competing with the model vendors, said Lane Irvine, director of strategic alliances for Calgary, Alberta-based Long View Systems, a longtime Cisco partner.
“They want to be the overseer of AI,” Irvine said.
Customers right now are mixing and matching AI models, and because they aren’t standardizing on one, the opportunity exists for an agnostic AI player. It’s similar to the approach that Cisco is taking with its Cloud Control agentic AI platform that became generally available earlier this year, he said.
“They’re going down the path of allowing [Cisco Cloud Control] to control third-party devices. ... They’ll have competitive [vendors] in there and want to be the platform for all of it,” Irvine said.

Cisco Announces Webex AI Agents for Meetings and Customer Service
Cisco announces Webex AI agents for meetings and customer service. Learn what IT teams should check about availability, integrations and access controls.
Cisco announced new Webex AI agent capabilities at WebexOne 2026, outlining plans for collaboration and customer-service workflows. Image: Cisco
Cisco wants AI agents to work inside Webex meetings, messages and customer-service workflows, giving IT teams new integration and oversight decisions.
Cisco announced new agentic capabilities at WebexOne on Oct. 7, designed to help AI agents use shared context and carry out multi-step tasks across collaboration and customer-service systems.
The announcements include Dialog for maintaining customer context across interactions and planned capabilities for agents to participate in Webex spaces, meetings and calls. Several features remain forthcoming
Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer at Cisco says that “the next era of work isn’t about bolting chatbots onto yesterday’s tools,” but rather “about AI agents working alongside people and teams.”
Cisco’s Webex is bringing together enterprise context, collaboration software and AI agents to its platform. The company is extending this idea beyond video conferencing into workplace management and customer service.
Cisco describes workflows in which employees could @mention an analytics agent in a Webex space to retrieve usage statistics, then ask a presentation agent to update a PowerPoint deck.
For customer service, Cisco introduced Dialog, a software layer connecting enterprise systems with the Webex AI Agent platform. Cisco says it is designed to maintain customer context across interactions and coordinate follow-up work after a conversation ends.
Cisco anticipates beta availability in the first quarter of calendar 2027, with release timing subject to change
Cisco says Claude, powered by Claude Managed Agents, will be able to join Webex spaces, meetings and calls. Separately, the Webex Suite Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration brings Webex context into OpenAI dots. Availability of dots within Webex is planned for a future release.
Connecting agents to multiple applications makes data permissions and oversight important deployment considerations.
Cisco says AI Agent 360 brings together agent security and monitoring capabilities, including Cisco AI Defense and Splunk observability. The newly announced Agent Observability with Splunk capability is planned for general availability in December 2026.
What IT Teams Should Check Before Deployment
IT teams should assess where these capabilities could improve existing workflows and what access controls and human oversight they would require.
For customer-service teams, agentic AI could reduce repetitive information gathering and help coordinate complex requests across multiple systems. Additionally, businesses could automate parts of workflows that currently require employees interacting with several cross-platform tools so as to accomplish a task.
Cisco has positioned agentic AI as a way to connect collaboration, workplace operations and customer service. For enterprises, the potential benefit is not simply having more AI tools. It is coordinating work across systems that have traditionally operated separately.
For IT teams, the next step is to identify a workflow worth testing, confirm feature availability and licensing, and define what agents can access or change. A limited pilot with human approval for sensitive actions would help organizations evaluate results before expanding deployment.
Read more: Learn why enterprise approval and audit controls matter when AI agents act across company systems.

Latest recognition reinforces WWT's role in helping customers build and secure AI infrastructure with full-stack innovation
ST. LOUIS, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--World Wide Technology (WWT), a global technology solutions provider, today announced it has earned the Cisco Secure AI Infrastructure Specialization in the United States. This achievement marks WWT's third major Cisco recognition in 2026, following its recognition as a Cisco Global Partner and earning the Cisco Secure Networking Specialization earlier this year. WWT is the only Cisco Global Partner to have earned both the Secure Networking and Secure AI Infrastructure Specializations in the U.S., underscoring the company's breadth of expertise across the full-stack, spanning networking, security, data center solutions and AI software.
The Secure AI Infrastructure Specialization is one of Cisco's new next-generation specializations, reserved for Cisco Preferred Partners with demonstrated expertise in designing, deploying and supporting secure AI infrastructure built on Cisco's industry-leading portfolio. To earn the specialization, WWT, in the U.S., completed a rigorous audit validating its people, processes and tools to deliver real customer outcomes as organizations move from AI experimentation to production at scale.
For WWT, this achievement contributes to a broader AI strategy, including work already underway with the Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA, an enterprise architecture combining scalable AI infrastructure with agent operations, observability and security that WWT helps operationalize for customers moving AI workloads into production. It also aligns to the goal of the Advanced Technology Center (ATC), where WWT's AI Proving Ground lets customers evaluate NVIDIA accelerated computing, storage and networking configurations before deployment, and the Cyber Range gives teams hands-on experience securing AI environments before those risks show up in production.
"Organizations deploying AI need partners that can bring together infrastructure, networking, security, observability and operations into a single, trusted architecture," said Joe Koenig, President, WWT. "Earning Cisco's Secure AI Infrastructure Specialization validates the investments we've made across our engineering talent, innovation platforms and partner ecosystems to help customers move AI from experimentation to secure production. WWT is proud to be the only Cisco partner to achieve the full set of these new distinctions."
"Customers are looking for trusted partners that can help them navigate the complexity of deploying AI securely and at scale," said Elisabeth De Dobbeleer, SVP, Global Partner Program GTM at Cisco. "WWT's achievement of the Cisco Secure AI Infrastructure Specialization demonstrates the technical expertise, operational excellence and customer focus required to help organizations build the secure AI foundations needed for long-term success."
The recognition reinforces years of work helping WWT clients operationalize secure AI environments through a broad technology ecosystem. This includes aligning Cisco's end-to-end AI security portfolio with all seven domains of ARMOR (AI Readiness Model for Operational Resilience), WWT's vendor-agnostic AI security framework. ARMOR's development has been shaped by critical feedback from early adopters, helping refine the strategic domain coverage and direction. Together, the domains provide customers with a practical framework for integrating governance, risk, compliance, model protection, infrastructure security, secure operations and data protection into a single, actionable structure.
WWT's Cisco partnership spans more than three decades with continued investment in the people, labs and processes needed to help customers navigate increasingly complex, AI-driven environments. To learn more about WWT's Cisco practice, visit wwt.com/partner/cisco.

Through its Advanced Technology Center (ATC), a collaborative ecosystem featuring state-of-the-art hardware and software, WWT enables clients and partners to conceptualize, test and validate innovative technology and then deploy solutions at scale using its global integration and distribution capabilities.
