Networking Stocks Rally as Tech Rebound Lifts AI Gear Makers: Ciena and Arista Climb 4%, but Cisco Barely Moves
AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

Cisco and NVIDIA Announce USFP: Expanding the Path to AI Connectivity
The Ultra-Dense Small Form-Factor Pluggable (USFP) is industry’s first pluggable form factor designed to help customers scale AI networks, providing a path to up to 12.8T of aggregate capacity while preserving proven deployment and serviceability models
As AI evolves from answering prompts to orchestrating complex, multi-step workflows, infrastructure demands are growing rapidly. From training and inference to emerging agentic AI systems, modern AI workloads depend on continuous communication across accelerators, applications, storage, and services, driving unprecedented requirements for bandwidth, responsiveness, and scale.
At Cisco, we believe the future of AI networking will be defined by how effectively silicon, systems, optics, software, and operations work together as a full-stack platform, enabling customers to scale AI with greater performance, efficiency, serviceability, and investment protection by optimizing every layer of the infrastructure together. Customers should not have to redesign their infrastructure or abandon established operational models to take advantage of the next generation of networking innovation.
Today, together with NVIDIA, we are announcing design plans for USFP, the industry’s first 400G-per-lane capable pluggable form factor designed to enable the next generation of AI Ethernet fabrics. USFP will provide a path supporting both 200G and 400G SerDes based systems and ASICs , helping customers scale from today’s 1.6T fabrics, with the ability to achieve 12.8T of overall pluggable capacity while preserving the benefits that have made pluggable optics successful.
As AI clusters grow across data centers, clouds, and edge environments, networks must carry significantly more traffic while balancing power, cooling, operational flexibility, and serviceability.
USFP is the next step in that journey. It addresses a critical industry challenge: delivering higher capacity AI fabrics without disrupting the manufacturing, deployment, and operational models that have enabled the scale and success of the pluggable ecosystem.
That perspective has shaped Cisco and NVIDIA’s collaboration for years. Together, we have helped customers build increasingly sophisticated infrastructure spanning networking, security, AI systems, and high-performance AI fabrics. Our work has been guided by a shared goal: helping customers accelerate AI adoption while maintaining flexibility, openness, and choice.
Preserving what works while advancing what’s next
The future of AI networking will not be defined by a single architectural approach. The industry continues to innovate across pluggable, near-packaged, co-packaged, and other emerging optical architectures, each with different advantages and tradeoffs. Customers will choose the technologies that best align with their operational requirements and long-term infrastructure strategies.
Organizations continue to value independently field replaceable modules, mature supply chains, interoperability across suppliers, and familiar serviceability models. These advantages become even more important as AI environments grow in scale and complexity.
USFP will extend those benefits into the next era of AI networking. It will provide a path toward higher capacity AI fabrics and higher density networking switch and compute equipment, while preserving the operational simplicity, openness, and ecosystem flexibility data center operators rely on today.
Accelerating the next generation of AI fabrics
USFP was designed with a simple objective: help AI networks scale efficiently.
With 16 lanes capable of operating at 400 Gb/s per lane, USFP will deliver 6.4T of aggregate capacity, four times the bandwidth density of today’s 1.6T pluggables. The architecture can scale to 32 lanes, providing a path to 12.8T of aggregate capacity. It also creates an opportunity for approximately 1.3x greater power efficiency through the use of 400G SerDes technology, helping operators manage growing power and cooling demands.
Together, these innovations create a foundation for higher-capacity AI Ethernet fabrics and continued innovation across the pluggable networking ecosystem.
To help customers scale AI infrastructure efficiently and sustainably, Cisco takes a full-stack, co-designed platform approach that combines silicon, high-density systems, optics, software, and operational expertise.
USFP reflects that philosophy. Rather than a standalone innovation, it is part of a broader platform vision that advances scale, efficiency, and performance while preserving the deployment, serviceability, and lifecycle models customers depend on.
USFP enables the industry to accelerate AI by building on the ecosystem models that have powered today’s AI networks. By combining a path to higher-capacity fabrics and improved efficiency with familiar operational practices, USFP helps customers scale AI infrastructure while maintaining the flexibility, interoperability, and consistency required at scale.
Cisco has long championed open ecosystems and industry collaboration to accelerate innovation and customer adoption. We see USFP as an extension of that approach, helping create a foundation for broad industry participation, interoperability, and long-term investment protection.
As AI networks continue to grow, Cisco and NVIDIA remain committed to delivering innovations that advance performance while preserving the operational foundations customers trust.

Price Prediction: Cisco Stock Will Trade at $200 on This Date
Cisco's AI order book has management calling it a networking supercycle, and shareholders want to know if a $200 share price is the payoff. A fresh model breaks down exactly how far the rally can realistically run and what stands…
Published October 19, 2026, 1:00pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
Depicting robust market activity and an upward trend, this graphic reflects the optimistic outlook for Cisco stock based on recent price predictions. © SylisiaDesign / Shutterstock.com
Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO | CSCO Price Prediction) has run hard on AI networking demand, and the obvious next question for shareholders is whether $200 a share is on the horizon. We modeled what a $1,000 investment could become by 2031, starting from a reference price of $113.64.
Shares were changing hands near $109.13 noon, down 3.97% on the session. With an AI order book that management calls a supercycle, Cisco deserves a fresh forward look.
Your $1,000 Could Reach About $1,563.50 by 2031
In the five-year base case, a $1,000 investment might reach roughly $1,563.50 by 2031, a total return of 56.35%. The estimate assumes a modeled share price of $177.67 on October 15, 2031, which works out to 9.35% a year.
Neither horizon in the model gets Cisco to $200. The highest target is the five-year bull case at $187.86. Getting to $200 from the reference price would take a gain of 75.9944%. That makes $200 an hypothetical stretch scenario beyond 2031. The model gives no date for it.
Bull, Base and Bear Scenarios for a $1,000 Stake
The model gives its forecast a confidence score of 0.9, which it rates as high. Wall Street’s consensus target is $136.16. The analyst count is 5 strong buys, 14 buys, 10 holds and 0 sells.
Three Drivers Behind Cisco’s Upside Case
Cisco took in $9.30B of AI orders in fiscal 2026 and guided AI infrastructure revenue to about $7.5B in fiscal 2027, up from roughly $4 billion. Chief Executive Chuck Robbins called it “a multi-year, multi-billion dollar networking super cycle.” In the fourth quarter, networking product orders grew 40% year over year.
Guidance Points to Faster Earnings Growth
Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $72.2B to $73.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $5.05 to $5.11, compared with $4.33 in fiscal 2026. The model works from forward EPS of $5.146 and a forward P/E of 22. A higher multiple on those earnings is how the long-term path gets built.
Consistent Beats and Steady Capital Returns
Cisco has exceeded EPS estimates for 6 consecutive quarters. Its latest report showed $1.22 against a $1.17 estimate, on revenue of $17.25B. Shareholders collect a $0.42 quarterly dividend, and $8.1B remains on the buyback authorization.
Margins are already under pressure. Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 66.3% from 68.4% as AI hardware took a larger share of the mix, and the CFO expects a slight drag in fiscal 2027. The AI growth story leans on hyperscaler capital spending, which can change fast (we covered seven of the suppliers riding that expansion, from power to networking, in a free report here).
Fiscal 2027 guidance already includes tariffs and a restructuring plan announced on May 13, 2026, and execution on both could fell. Geopolitics and supply constraints add further uncertainty.
The stock is also volatile. Shares are up 61.84% over the past year but down 7.04% over the past week, and the 52-week high is $129.38.
Retail view is also marked as bearish. The next test comes with the fiscal first-quarter earnings report on November 12, 2026, where guidance calls for revenue of $18.0B to $18.2B.
By 2031, the model puts a $1,000 Cisco investment somewhere between $1,063.80 and $1,653.10, with $1,563.50 as the base case. A $200 share price stands above even the bull case, so it remains outside the modeled outcomes. The modeled scenarios above do not constitute investment advice.

How Much Of Cisco Stock's Rise Did The Business Earn?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:02 AM CDT 4 min read
Cisco Systems (CSCO) supplies businesses and the hyperscalers building AI infrastructure with networking and security products, along with services. The company's stock climbed 92% between late July 2021 and mid-October 2026, before dividends. A rally of that magnitude makes it natural to credit a growing business. So take a guess: how much of that rise came from Cisco selling more?
How Much Did Cisco's Sales Grow?
Cisco expanded its sales 27% over those five years. The company generated $63.3 billion in the twelve months to July 2026, compared with $49.8 billion in the twelve months to July 2021. That growth accounts for a little over a third of the stock's rise. Because the four changes multiply together, each portion of the rise is measured on a scale that lets them add up to 100%.
Expanding the business represents a real achievement. Yet nearly two thirds of the stock's advance came from somewhere else.
What Else Lifted Cisco Stock?
As the table details, most of the remaining gain came from what investors pay for Cisco's profit.
The price-to-earnings multiple, representing what investors pay for each dollar of profit, served as the largest source. Cisco's multiple rose from 22.1 to 32.0, and that expansion provided more than half of the stock's overall gain. The company also kept repurchasing stock, including during its latest quarter. The share count fell 5.8%, which added about a tenth of the rise. Meanwhile, Cisco's net margin, the share of sales the company keeps as profit, slipped slightly and pulled the price down a little.
So investors assigning a higher value to Cisco's profit did more for the stock than business growth did.
Can Margins And Multiples Keep Rising?
Multiples and margins cannot expand indefinitely, whereas sales can increase for as long as Cisco keeps selling more. The company's margin sat at 21.0% over the latest twelve months. That figure stands below the 26% it reached over the twelve months to the third quarter of fiscal 2019, marking its high for the past ten years.
By contrast, the multiple sits higher today than it did at 36 of the 40 quarter ends since fiscal 2017. The lift Cisco received from its multiple is therefore unlikely to repeat the way sales growth can.
What Cisco Would Need To Repeat Its Rise
If the margin, the multiple and the share count remained where they are, Cisco's sales would need to grow about 13.3% a year for the next five and a quarter years to give the stock the same rise. That future timeframe matches the window of the stock's historical rally. Over the past five years, Cisco grew sales 4.9% a year.
Sales are growing faster now. Sales rose 11.8% in fiscal 2026 and 17.6% in the quarter to July 2026. The Networking business led the expansion, growing 22.5% for the year. Management said about 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue came from AI infrastructure for hyperscalers, up from less than 2% in fiscal 2025.
Measured against the pace required for a repeat performance, Cisco's sales growth is the figure to watch in its next report, expected on or around November 10, 2026.
Does This Mean You Should Act On CSCO?
Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.
There is a smarter approach. Since its inception, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has returned 105%, beating the benchmark that combines the three major indices - the S&P 500, S&P Mid-cap, and Russell 2000. And it did so without taking the concentrated risk that comes with do-it-yourself stock picking. If that is how you want to invest, the HQ Portfolio is the place to start.

Prediction: Cisco Stock Could Surprise Wall Street by 2030
Cisco's CEO is calling it a networking super cycle, and the numbers behind that claim are hard to ignore. But reaching $200 by 2030 requires three specific things to go right, and at least one of them sits outside the…
Published October 17, 2026, 10:30am ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
© Alexander Koerner / Getty Images News via Getty Images
Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO | CSCO Price Prediction | CSCO Price Prediction) sits in the middle of what its CEO calls a networking super cycle. Last quarter, product revenue rose 24% to $13.46B and networking climbed 28% to $9.79B. AI orders reached $9.30B for fiscal 2026.
Shares are up 43.91% YTD, yet they trade at $108.87 after a 4.2% drop today. Chuck Robbins said it directly: “We believe we’re only at the beginning of this super cycle.” So can Cisco reach $200 by 2030?
The stock has lost momentum. Shares fell 7.26% over the past week and 0.71% over the past month. They now trade below the 52-week high of $129.38. Investors are focused on margins.
Non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 66.3% from 68.4% as lower-margin AI hardware took a bigger share of sales. Management also highlighted memory costs and uneven hyperscaler order timing. With a beta of 0.979, Cisco usually tracks the broader market, which makes a sharp one-day drop a clear sign of investor nerves.
Wall Street Sees 25.1% Upside. Our Model Says 19.5%
The consensus target is $136.16, an upside of 25.1%. It rests on 5 Strong Buy, 14 Buy, 10 Hold and 0 Sell ratings. Our one-year base case is $130.14, a 19.5% gain. The scenarios run from $109.27 in the bear case to $138.12 in the bull case, and model confidence is high at 0.9.
In my view, both expectations underestimate Cisco’s earnings. Earnings grew 52.1% year over year, yet only 66% of analysts rate the stock bullish. Ten Holds on a company guiding to $5.05 to $5.11 in fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS strike me as too conservative.
Here’s What It Takes for Cisco to Reach $200
To get to $200 from today’s price of $108.87 would require a gain of 83.7%.
With forward EPS of $5.146, a price of $200 implies a forward P/E of 39x. Our base case of $130.14 already implies 26x, so the bold target requires 13x of additional multiple expansion.
Today’s valuation looks steep, but the math shifts over time. If EPS compounds at the 9.23% consensus growth rate through fiscal 2030, it reaches about $6.71, and $200 works out to roughly 30x.
Earnings growth does most of the lifting. An adjustment factor of 1.125 reflects technology sector momentum and strong earnings acceleration, with the five-year bull case already reaching $187.86.
The catalysts keep coming. Cisco expects AI infrastructure revenue of $7.5B in fiscal 2027, roughly double fiscal 2026. Recent releases highlighted Splunk advancements for trusted AI, new agentic collaboration experiences and scalability and openness at OCP 2026.
Robbins added: “The network remains an absolute critical factor as to whether AI deployments succeed or fail.” Cisco is one of several picks-and-shovels names gaining from the data-center expansion (we rounded up seven of these AI infrastructure suppliers, networking included, in a free report here).
A major risk is that hyperscaler AI spending cools before enterprise demand can fill the gap.
Where Cisco Trades Today vs Its Earnings Power
At $108.87, Cisco trades at 21x forward EPS. That’s a reasonable multiple for a company guiding to $72.2B to $73.4B in fiscal 2027 revenue, up from $63.33B in fiscal 2026.
Shares sit between a 52-week low of $67.32 and a high of $129.38. Over 10 years, the stock has returned 383.19%. A 21x multiple on accelerating earnings leaves room for the bull case to play out.
$200 Is a Stretch, But Here’s Why It’s Possible
Hitting $200 by 2030 would take an 83.7% gain. I see it as a stretch, though a reachable one. Three things need to go right. AI infrastructure revenue has to keep growing past $7.5B. Security growth needs to improve to high single digits, as management expects. Operating margins also have to hold near 35% while gross margin slips.
A sharp pullback in hyperscaler capex would undermine the thesis. Returns at this level shouldn’t be expected every year, but we’ve outlined the path for how Cisco could reach $200 in 2030.

Cisco vs. IBM: Why the Stock Nobody Wants Could Be the Better Retirement Buy
One tech giant is up over 50% this year while the other has fallen out of favor with Wall Street, and for retirees living off dividend income, that divergence points toward a clear winner that most investors are overlooking.
Published October 13, 2026, 11:45am ET · 3 min read
Abstract financial data graph featuring candlestick and line charts © Abstract financial data graph featuring candlestick and line charts (Shutterstock.com) by hateeyes
Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO | CSCO Price Prediction) or IBM (NYSE:IBM): which tech dividend stock makes the stronger case for a retirement-focused investor right now? Cisco is the momentum story. It is up 52.27% year to date on an AI networking boom. IBM is the yield story, down 19.88% year to date after a second-quarter earnings miss. For income, the stock that has fallen out of favor has the stronger case.
IBM’s quarterly dividend of $1.69 works out to a 2.91% yield at the current $232.58 share price. Cisco’s $0.42 quarterly payout yields just 1.46% at $115.19. Cisco’s own rally caused the gap. The stock is up 72.64% over the past year, which contracted its yield. Put the same dollars into IBM and you collect about twice the income. Winner: IBM.
Dividend Safety: IBM’s Cash Cushion Runs Deeper
IBM generated $14.73 billion in free cash flow in 2025, up 25.29%, and paid $6.255 billion in dividends. That means the dividend used only 42% of free cash flow. Even in the quarter that missed estimates, free cash flow rose 70.36% to $2.54 billion.
Cisco’s fiscal 2026 operating cash flow of $14.177 billion, minus $1.41 billion in capital spending, left about $12.77 billion. Dividends of $6.553 billion took 51% of that. Add buybacks and total capital returns reached 99% of free cash flow. Buybacks give Cisco room to adjust, but the dividend has a thinner buffer.
Cisco does win on earnings coverage. Its dividend is 39% of fiscal 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $4.33, compared with 60% of IBM’s trailing EPS of $11.25. IBM also carries $61.3 billion in debt and faces a securities fraud inquiry. Still, companies pay dividends with cash, and IBM has more cash to spare. Winner: IBM.
Dividend Growth: Cisco Raises Much Faster
IBM just raised its dividend for the 31st consecutive year, and its dividend record going back to 1999 shows a higher payout every year. The raises are small, though. The quarterly payout went from $1.64 in 2021 to $1.69 today, a gain of just 3%. Cisco, on its 15th consecutive annual increase, went from $0.37 to $0.42 over the same stretch, up 13.5%.
Cisco’s business supports faster raises. Fiscal 2027 EPS guidance is $5.05 to $5.11, and the company expects AI infrastructure revenue to about double to $7.5 billion. IBM’s mainframe revenue fell 42% in the second quarter and operating income dropped 19.67%. Its chief executive now expects “constant currency revenue growth in the range of four-to-five percent”. Winner: Cisco.
Verdict: IBM Is the Retiree’s Income Stock
IBM comes out on top in two of three categories, and both wins matter most to someone living off dividends. A 2.91% yield supported by a 42% free cash flow payout puts more cash in a retiree’s pocket every quarter. A beta of 0.724 means less volatility. The selloff also brought down the price. IBM trades at a forward P/E of 17, while Cisco sits near 27 times fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings. Barron’s wrote that IBM stock looks cheap, but Wall Street isn’t buying it yet.
Cisco makes the stronger case for investors a decade or more from retirement. They can accept a thin yield today in exchange for faster dividend growth and AI-driven gains in the share price. For a retiree who needs income now, IBM is the stronger stock, and the broader goal of living off the checks without selling shares is the whole basis of a free dividend ladder guide we put together here. Watch IBM’s next quarterly report for signs of a mainframe recovery and news on the fraud inquiry. For Cisco, the test is whether fiscal first-quarter revenue lands within its $18.0 billion to $18.2 billion guidance.

Cisco (CSCO): Can Its Earnings Recovery Turn Into Lasting Cash Growth?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:07 AM CDT 5 min read
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) has an opportunity to turn artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending and network upgrades into stronger cash generation. Fiscal-2026 net income increased 30% to $13.3 billion, but operating cash flow stayed near $14.2 billion. Reported earnings also benefited from higher unrealized investment gains, which increased profit without generating operating cash. Cisco's cybersecurity business adds another growth avenue as companies strengthen their defenses against evolving threats. Find our rankings of cybersecurity stocks here.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) trades at approximately 20x forward earnings and 32x trailing earnings. The earnings outlook combines operating growth with accounting exclusions. Fiscal-2027 guidance calls for GAAP EPS of $4.00–$4.06, against $3.33 in fiscal 2026, and company-defined non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $5.05–$5.11. Adjustments include stock compensation, acquisition-related amortization, and restructuring. The lower forward multiple should not be read as pure profit growth.
Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) is the closest operating comparison because it competes in network switching. Its 45.4% second-quarter GAAP operating margin sets a high profitability benchmark for Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO). Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE) has greater server exposure, and its inventory commitments create a different cash-conversion test. The 20x forward valuation looks reasonable only if its fourth-quarter cash rebound persists.
Installed Networks Support Growth, but Require Funding
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) benefits from established enterprise networks, customer relationships, and the cost of replacing integrated equipment and software. Management says more than half its customers purchase both campus and data-center networking. That breadth creates opportunities to sell upgrades into existing relationships and spread development and support expenses across more revenue. Billionaire Ken Fisher also holds a position in Cisco, reflecting investor interest in the networking company. See which other AI stocks are on the billionaire's radar.
AI demand strengthens that opportunity. Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) booked $9.3 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and recognized about $4 billion in associated revenue. Management expects $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue in fiscal 2027. The difference between bookings and sales matters because large AI orders can arrive well before shareholder cash.
Revenue guidance of $72.2 billion–$73.4 billion implies approximately 15% growth at the midpoint. The adjusted EPS midpoint implies about 17% growth from fiscal-2026 adjusted EPS of $4.33. Those forecasts require operating leverage as shipments increase, while memory shortages and higher component prices can absorb part of the benefit.
Subscription revenue gives Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) a recurring base, but it increased only about 1% to $32.0 billion in fiscal 2026. Maintaining that base supports investment; it does not yet establish accelerating software cash growth. Hardware expansion still requires inventory purchases before customer payments arrive, and competitive pricing can limit the profit retained from additional shipments.
A Better Quarter Has Not Removed the Cash Burden
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $5.4 billion of fourth-quarter operating cash flow, up 27%. That is meaningful evidence against treating the annual cash plateau as permanent. Fiscal 2026 also included the final $2.3 billion U.S. transition-tax payment, removing one specific future cash obligation.
Working capital nevertheless remains demanding. Annual inventory and financing-receivable movements absorbed approximately $2.5 billion and $1.8 billion, respectively. Both continued consuming cash in the fourth quarter, when their combined use approached $2.8 billion. Higher deferred revenue and other liabilities helped offset those demands. The rebound did not come from releasing inventory or collecting down customer financing.
Offering payment flexibility can support equipment sales, but customer financing earns its keep only when collections justify the risk. Persistently larger financing balances would tie up capital and reduce the cash available for distributions, even if reported sales and earnings continued growing.
Non-GAAP free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment, declined 4% to $12.8 billion as capital spending increased. Dividends and buybacks consumed approximately 99% of that amount. Sustaining distributions alongside growth investment therefore depends on better conversion, not simply higher accounting profit.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) produced $13.3 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2025 before the latest decline. The business has demonstrated substantial cash generation, but stronger AI demand now brings heavier funding requirements. At 20x forward earnings, shareholders need growth that increases cash after those commitments. More sales alone would provide little valuation protection if funding needs absorbed the additional profit.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) looks reasonably valued at 20x forward earnings if the fourth-quarter cash recovery becomes sustained growth. Installed relationships and stronger infrastructure demand make that outcome credible. It requires earnings growth to produce more cash after investment, with inventory and financing needs growing more slowly than sales. Continued working-capital expansion alongside flat free cash flow would make the valuation demanding, even if orders remained strong.
While we acknowledge the potential of CSCO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Cisco Could Be Entering a New Growth Phase. Here’s My Price Target.
Cisco just posted its fifth straight earnings beat while AI infrastructure orders piled up, but the real question is whether the valuation still leaves room to run or whether this rally has already priced in the upside.
Published October 8, 2026, 7:15am ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This graphic illustrates the interconnectedness of advanced optical technology, like that developed by Lumentum, with significant market and investment growth. © Shutterstock
The 24/7 Wall St. price target for Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO | CSCO Price Prediction) is $132.90 over the next 12 months. Shares trade at $117.71 this morning, so the target means 12.9% upside. The model gives Cisco a buy rating with high confidence.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
Cisco has changed from a slow-growth dividend payer into one of the cleaner ways to own AI networking. Our target sits a bit below the consensus analyst target of $136.16 because the model reduces mega-cap upside on purpose. Even so, it points higher from here.
AI Orders Fueled a 55.6% Rally This Year
Cisco is up 10.48% over the past week, 8.2% over the past month and 55.6% year to date. Shares sit 9% below the 52-week high of $129.38 and 79.4% above the low of $65.60.
Fiscal Q4 revenue came in at $17.25 billion, up 17.6% and ahead of the $16.83 billion estimate. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 exceeded the $1.17 consensus, Cisco’s fifth straight beat. AI infrastructure orders reached $9.3 billion for fiscal 2026. Management forecast fiscal 2027 revenue to $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion and EPS to $5.05 to $5.11.
Our bull case reaches $139.29. Hyperscaler AI revenue is expected to hit $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027. Cisco also holds three P200 scale-across design wins, and Wi-Fi 7 now makes up more than 50% of wireless orders.
CEO Chuck Robbins said, “We believe we’re only at the beginning of this super cycle.” Analysts agree: 5 rate Cisco a Strong Buy, 14 a Buy and 9 a Hold, and none rate it a Sell.
Our bear case comes to at $110.74. Non-GAAP gross margin slid to 66.3% from 68.4%, and the CFO warned of “a slight gross margin headwind” through fiscal 2027.
Price increases added about five points to Q4 growth, which flatters volume. To be fair, operating margin still rose to 35.9% from 34.3%. Cash fell 23.8%, but that reflects $12.7 billion returned to shareholders.
Cisco Looks Cheap Next to Arista and HPE
Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) is Cisco’s most direct AI data-center rival. Arista increased revenue 37.69% last quarter but trades at 77x earnings. Cisco trades at an implied 27x trailing and 23x forward earnings.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) is now a larger enterprise networking rival after buying Juniper Networks. Its networking revenue increased 74.9%, a figure raised by the deal, while its non-GAAP operating margin was 16.2%. The 24/7 Wall St. price target looks conservative against both peers.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $132.90 comes with a buy rating and 90% confidence. What tips the scale for me is AI growth at a valuation far below Arista’s (we rounded up seven companies driving the AI data-center expansion, from power to networking, which you can find here).
The setup strengthens if hyperscaler AI revenue tracks toward $7.5 billion while operating margin holds near 35%. It weakens if gross margin compression speeds up or hyperscaler orders stall. On the current data, Cisco’s new growth phase looks real.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target model projects where Cisco could trade, assuming current growth and market conditions hold.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
The projections assume Cisco keeps executing on Silicon One, optics and security. Big moves either way could come from changes in hyperscaler capital spending or tariff policy.

Cisco (CSCO): Can Software Renewals Outlast the Networking Upgrade Cycle?
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 1:20 PM CDT 4 min read
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) sells networking equipment, software, and support to enterprises and service providers. AI infrastructure spending and campus upgrades are lifting demand. The question is how much customers will keep paying after equipment purchases slow. As an established networking leader, Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) is among the 10 Most Active Blue Chip Stocks to Buy Right Now.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) trades at 20x forward P/E and 32x trailing P/E. Its premium to Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE), at 14x forward P/E, requires durable renewal profits and cash generation.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) packages network-management capabilities with hardware and software support. Standard new subscriptions have a three-year minimum term and multiple feature tiers. Older equipment still needs software updates and troubleshooting. Familiar tools and trained staff support retention by making switching disruptive.
For supported switches, basic capabilities and manual patching remain perpetual, while automated patching and software-image management require subscriptions. Labor savings and reduced downtime must exceed renewal costs to support pricing.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE) is expanding its combined Aruba and Juniper Mist offering, which could pressure renewal pricing during campus upgrades.
Higher Expected Profits Explain Part of the Gap
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) trades at 20x forward P/E and 32x trailing P/E; trailing P/E reflects past earnings while forward P/E uses forecasts. Management expects fiscal 2027 GAAP EPS of $4.00–$4.06, versus $3.33 in fiscal 2026. Lower expected taxes also support growth: guidance assumes a 14.5% GAAP tax rate, versus 17.1% in fiscal 2026. Meanwhile, $1.39 billion of pretax net investment gains lifted fiscal 2026 reported earnings. Company-defined non-GAAP profits exclude stock compensation, acquired-intangible amortization and restructuring. Sustainable earnings require operating gains beyond tax benefits and investment returns.
A Higher Multiple Needs Durable Earnings
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) carries a 20x forward P/E, compared with 17x in 2025. Stronger AI networking demand and higher earnings expectations support the increase. Maintaining that premium requires profitable software revenue after the equipment upgrade wave fades.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) reported companywide annualized recurring revenue, or ARR, of $32.1 billion, up 3%, while fiscal fourth-quarter networking revenue rose 28%. ARR measures the annualized revenue run rate of active contracts, including subscriptions and maintenance. It does not isolate networking renewals from initial sales. Retention and customer expansion show how existing accounts contribute to growth.
Management says AI-assisted support is improving renewal rates. Lower service costs would make renewals more profitable, provided discounts and cheaper tiers do not erode those savings.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE:HPE) is the closest broad enterprise-networking comparator through Aruba and Juniper, although servers and storage change its business mix. Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) earned a 24.7% quarterly GAAP operating margin, versus its peer's 11.4%. That margin advantage supports a premium. Its adjusted EPS guidance implies approximately 17% growth for the fiscal year ending July 2027. Separately, the peer targets 16%–20% growth for the year ending October 2027.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $14.2 billion of fiscal 2026 operating cash flow, essentially unchanged, while inventory increased to $5.7 billion from $3.2 billion. Hardware expansion absorbs working capital. Renewals could improve cash generation without comparable inventory investment. Investors should track renewal pricing, downgrades, and service margins, consistent with testing subscription growth against underlying profitability.
Higher memory costs and a heavier hardware mix reduced quarterly adjusted product gross margin by 2.7 percentage points. Software can offset that pressure when incremental revenue exceeds hosting, development and support costs. Discounted renewals could preserve customer numbers while weakening earnings, limiting how much of the business deserves a premium for recurring earnings.
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) can justify 20x forward earnings if renewals preserve pricing and improve cash generation as hardware growth slows. Higher margins support the premium, but recurring profits must survive stronger competition. For investors assessing 10 Most Active Blue Chip Stocks to Buy, persistent downgrades or rising service costs would weaken the case for paying that premium.
While we acknowledge the potential of CSCO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Three Drivers Behind Cisco's Upside Case
Cisco took in $9.30B of AI orders in fiscal 2026 and guided AI infrastructure revenue to about $7.5B in fiscal 2027, up from roughly $4 billion. Chief Executive Chuck Robbins called it "a multi-year, multi-billion dollar networking super cycle." In the fourth quarter, networking product orders grew 40% year over year.
Guidance Points to Faster Earnings Growth
Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $72.2B to $73.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $5.05 to $5.11, compared with $4.33 in fiscal 2026. The model works from forward EPS of $5.146 and a forward P/E of 22. A higher multiple on those earnings is how the long-term path gets built.
Consistent Beats and Steady Capital Returns
Cisco has exceeded EPS estimates for 6 consecutive quarters. Its latest report showed $1.22 against a $1.17 estimate, on revenue of $17.25B. Shareholders collect a $0.42 quarterly dividend, and $8.1B remains on the buyback authorization.
Margins are already under pressure. Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 66.3% from 68.4% as AI hardware took a larger share of the mix, and the CFO expects a slight drag in fiscal 2027. The AI growth story leans on hyperscaler capital spending, which can change fast (we covered seven of the suppliers riding that expansion, from power to networking, in a free report here).
Fiscal 2027 guidance already includes tariffs and a restructuring plan announced on May 13, 2026, and execution on both could fell. Geopolitics and supply constraints add further uncertainty.
The stock is also volatile. Shares are up 61.84% over the past year but down 7.04% over the past week, and the 52-week high is $129.38.
Retail view is also marked as bearish. The next test comes with the fiscal first-quarter earnings report on November 12, 2026, where guidance calls for revenue of $18.0B to $18.2B.
By 2031, the model puts a $1,000 Cisco investment somewhere between $1,063.80 and $1,653.10, with $1,563.50 as the base case. A $200 share price stands above even the bull case, so it remains outside the modeled outcomes. The modeled scenarios above do not constitute investment advice.

Piper Sandler cuts Cisco price target to $125 on growth peak fears
Cisco stock shed nearly 5% on Tuesday after Piper Sandler analyst James Fish cut the firm's price target on the networking equipment company to $125 from $132, while holding a Neutral rating in place.
Fish and his team pointed to reduced price-to-earnings multiple assumptions, with the analysts expressing concern that the industry's growth trajectory may be approaching its ceiling, according to CNBC. Cisco stock closed Tuesday at $106.44.
On Wall Street, Cisco holds a consensus Buy rating, and analysts' average price target stands at $133.86, according to Benzinga. Also on the analyst front, Deutsche Bank started coverage with a Buy rating and a $135 price target on September 1, while HSBC moved to a Hold rating with a $120 target on August 14, Benzinga reported.
Shares reached an all-time peak in June and have gained 57% over the past year, buoyed by revenue growth tied to surging artificial intelligence investment.
The Piper Sandler move comes roughly a month after Cisco reported fourth-quarter revenue of $17.25 billion, beating analyst expectations and posting record annual results, though Cisco stock fell in after-hours trading following that announcement. For the full fiscal year 2026, revenue reached $63.3 billion, up 12%, with GAAP net income of $13.3 billion.
Cisco's guidance for fiscal year 2027 projected revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, implying nearly 15% growth. Skeptical analysts countered that underlying sales expansion would retreat to single-digit territory. Piper Sandler described the company's own outlook as "conservative" relative to what broader market demand would support, according to CNBC.
Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins addressed the cautious tone on guidance last month. "We're starting a new fiscal year. We're operating in incredible markets," Robbins told CNBC's Jim Cramer. "But it's also a time that we're going to start the year being a little bit prudent."
Hyperscalers — the major cloud and internet platforms driving infrastructure buildouts — accounted for roughly $4 billion of Cisco's revenue in fiscal 2026, and the company anticipates that contribution will nearly double to $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027.

Investors therefore need to distinguish temporary distribution timing from a payout policy that persistently exceeds cash generation.
For illustration purposes only: a semiconductor manufacturing facility.
Combined dividends and repurchases consumed 88.9% of annual free cash flow. Repurchases offer discretion if the cycle weakens, making total shareholder returns more flexible than a fixed obligation.
In a simple stress case, a 20% decline in annual free cash flow would leave $3.02 billion. Maintaining the same $3.35 billion distribution would then require $334 million from existing resources or financing. Cutting repurchases could close the gap. This is a policy sensitivity, not an earnings forecast.
Dividends alone consumed $1.06 billion, leaving $2.71 billion of annual free cash flow before repurchases. Under the same 20% cash decline, the dividend would still be covered 2.8 times. The combined payout can therefore become uncovered well before the dividend does. The first adjustment available to management is the pace of discretionary purchases, rather than an immediate need to cut the dividend.

Coverage doesn’t establish the right repurchase price

Semiconductor equipment stocks are giving back ground after a strong year powered by artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT | AMAT Price Prediction) stock is at $461.91, down 7% in afternoon trading, a pullback that still leaves it up 80% year to date. Selling is greatest among the companies that build chipmaking tools, a narrow corner of the chip trade.
Meanwhile, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) stock is trading at $297.04, down 4%, a smaller decline than the one hitting Applied Materials stock. Likewise, KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) shares are slipping 4% to $182.44, keeping pace with Lam Research stock.
Chip stocks as a group are holding up far better. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is down 1%. Over in large-cap tech, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.5%, a much softer reading than anything in the equipment group.
Applied Materials Gives Back Gains After EPIC Center Debut
Applied Materials stock is giving back part of a large advance, with the decline running alongside its equipment peers. One session earlier, the company unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center, known as the EPIC Center, at its Sunnyvale campus. Management describes the site as the world’s largest facility for collaborative semiconductor process and equipment research. Applied Materials expects capital spending there to scale to approximately $5 billion as customer projects begin.
A leading chipmaker joined the center as a founding partner, giving the project a strong start. Recent results also support the longer-term story. In August, Applied Materials reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $3.50 against a $3.39 estimate and guided Q4 FY2026 revenue to about $10.25 billion.
Equipment Makers Slide Harder Than the Broader Chip Group
All three equipment names carry large gains into the pullback, with Lam Research stock up 74% year to date and KLA stock up 51%. Each is falling several times harder than the semiconductor fund that holds them, a split that points at fabrication spending intentions, because the iShares fund also owns chip designers and foundries and its decline serves as broad sector context.
The EPIC Center commits capital to exactly the advanced-node and packaging work that AI buildouts require, and it ties major customers to Applied Materials earlier in the design cycle. In Q3 FY2026, U.S. customers accounted for 15% of Applied Materials’ revenue, while China fell to 28% from 35%. Looking further out, Applied Materials’ chief executive stated in the August results release, “Based on the increased demand visibility we are receiving from our customers, we expect another strong growth year for Applied Materials in 2027.”
Yet, equipment orders are discretionary, and a stock carrying a year-to-date gain of that size has a long way to fall whenever that spending is questioned. Policy adds another layer of risk, since China still made up a large share of Applied Materials’ revenue last quarter. Even after the pullback, Applied Materials shares hold most of their gain for the year, which leaves room for further profit-taking if spending plans shift.
Investors should track whether customer projects at the EPIC Center begin on schedule, since that work supports the bull case. A widening gap between the equipment trio and the iShares fund could signal deeper worries about fabrication budgets, while a narrowing gap could suggest the selling is fading.
Trading in Lam Research stock and KLA stock offers a useful cross-check, since both companies sell into the same fabrication budgets. Investors should keep their positions sized to that kind of volatility.

KLAC Surges 64.5% in a Year: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:26 AM CDT 5 min read
KLA KLAC shares have surged 64.5% over the past year, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector increase of 25.6% and the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry rise of 32.5%.
The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, which include ASML Holding ASML, Advanced Energy AEIS and Entegris ENTG. All three companies are expanding their footprint in the semiconductor industry. ASML Holding, Advanced Energy and Entegris shares have soared 63.4%, 37.3% and 61.8%, respectively, over the past year.
The outperformance can be attributed to strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging. These factors are helping KLAC fend off its competitors such as ASML Holding, Advanced Energy and Entegris.
KLAC Benefits From Strong Semiconductor Demand
KLAC is benefiting from accelerating investments in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, driven by rising AI computing requirements, growing adoption of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and increasing complexity in leading-edge chip manufacturing. The company's strong position in semiconductor process control, wafer inspection and metrology solutions has been a major growth driver.
In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Process Control revenues rose 13% to $3.26 billion, accounting for approximately 89% of total revenues. The segment benefited from continued investments in leading-edge manufacturing and increasing process control intensity across advanced semiconductor technologies.
AI infrastructure remains a major growth catalyst. Increasing AI compute requirements, hyperscale data-center investments, HBM adoption and sophisticated packaging architectures require tighter process control to improve yields and accelerate production ramps. KLA highlighted that customer demand signals have strengthened materially, while visibility continues to improve. The company expects business momentum to accelerate through the second half of 2026 and significant growth to continue in 2027.
Advanced packaging provides another significant growth opportunity. KLA now expects advanced packaging process-control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year and exceeding its previous expectation of high-50% growth. Meanwhile, Specialty Process, PCB and Component Inspection businesses are expected to grow more than 25% in calendar year 2026, supported by high-performance computing and greater package complexity.
The broader semiconductor equipment environment also remains favorable. KLA raised its calendar year 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market estimate, including advanced packaging, to the low-$150-billion range from its previous expectation of more than $140 billion. Broad-based investment across leading-edge logic, foundry, DRAM, HBM, NAND and advanced packaging is expected to sustain capacity expansion. KLA expects second-half 2026 revenues to increase roughly 20% from the first half.
KLAC's Expanding Backlog Strengthens Growth Prospects
KLAC is benefiting from a rapidly expanding backlog, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments and robust demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
KLA's backlog stood at about $12.6 billion, up roughly 60% from fiscal 2025, while the company said the order funnel remains strong. Customer shipment visibility extends through 2027 and, in some cases, into early 2028. Orders generally cover a 12–18-month delivery window, giving investors better visibility into future revenue despite the industry's cyclicality.
KLAC's strong exposure to AI-driven semiconductor investments is expected to benefit the company's top-line growth.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, KLA expects revenues of $4 billion (plus or minus $200 million). Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be $1.16 per share (plus or minus 10 cents). Foundry/logic is expected to account for about 73% of Semiconductor Process Control systems revenues to semiconductor customers, with memory at roughly 27%. Within memory, DRAM is projected to be about 90% and NAND at 10%. Non-GAAP operating expenses are anticipated to be approximately $690 million.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for KLAC's fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenues is pegged at $4.05 billion, suggesting growth of 26.09% year over year.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings is pegged at $1.18 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This indicates 34.09% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, KLAC is trading at 12.37X, higher than the broader sector's 6.03X.

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

One Reason KLA Stock Looks Better Than Its Price
Most investors still view KLA (KLAC) as a traditional wafer inspection company. However, the business selling inspection tools for advanced packaging is beginning to stand out, and management ties this demand to the expansion of AI. Packaging may be part of what buyers are currently paying for. The stock costs 51.4 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500, yet overall sales grew 15% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026. A price that high beside that growth rate presents a clear contradiction. So, how big has KLA's packaging business become?
KLA's Packaging Forecast: About $1.1 Billion In Calendar 2026
Management expects about $1.1 billion of revenue from packaging process control systems in calendar 2026. That figure represents an increase of more than 70% from a year earlier. The company provided this raised forecast during its fiscal Q4 2026 call on July 28, 2026, stepping up from an earlier expectation of growth in the high 50% range.
Management stated that the expansion of AI requires new, complex packaging steps, alongside additional KLA systems to bring those processes to high-volume production. Furthermore, customers adopting newer packaging methods such as hybrid bonding are buying more inspection tools, the company said.
Packaging remains a small fraction of the overall business at KLA, which recorded $13.6 billion in sales over the last twelve months. Yet management expects this segment to grow more than 70% in calendar 2026.
Does Packaging Help KLA With Rising Costs?
Not directly. While packaging brings KLA more sales, the segment does not alter what the company pays for parts.
Costs surfaced repeatedly on the July 28 call. KLA is buying memory components at higher prices, and management indicated those headwinds will "likely continue through next year." When asked why the company could not simply raise its own prices to match, executives explained that it is difficult to adjust pricing on existing orders. Instead, new prices are established when new products come out.
Despite these material costs, gross margin reached 62.4% in fiscal Q4 2026, landing at the upper end of KLA's guidance. Looking ahead to the September quarter, which KLA has yet to report, management forecast 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point.
Sales are also expanding. Management listed advanced packaging among the factors behind its record fiscal Q4 revenue of $3.66 billion. The company then guided to $4 billion for the September quarter, plus or minus $200 million.
Can KLA Build Its Tools Fast Enough?
Not during the first half of calendar 2026. Management noted that shortages of some long-lead-time materials held the company back during that period. If You Invested $1000 in KLA a Decade Ago, This is How Much It'd Be Worth Now
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

What if you'd invested in KLA (KLAC) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to KLAC for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?
With that in mind, let's take a look at KLA's main business drivers.
Milpitas, CA-based KLA Corporation is an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of process diagnostics and control (PDC) equipment and yield management solutions required for the fabrication of semiconductor integrated circuits (ICs) or chips. The company has a comprehensive portfolio of products addressing each major PDC subsegment, including photomask or reticle inspection, wafer inspection and defect review, and metrology.
Reticle production is vital to the semiconductor device formation process. Reticles control the precise deposition of materials onto the wafer, which changes its chemical characteristics and imparts specific functions to the ICs created. Inspection and metrology tools measure reticle quality and help improve production yields. The broader use of semiconductors, shrinking form factors and greater chip functionality continue to increase the importance of reticle design and production. Taiwan Semiconductor was the only largest customers in the last three years, accounting for more than 10% of total sales in fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024.
KLA reported revenues of $13.58 billion in fiscal 2026. Product revenues accounted for 77% of total revenues, while service revenues represented 23%. Semiconductor Process Control generated $12.24 billion, or 90% of fiscal 2026 revenues. Specialty Semiconductor Process and PCB and Component Inspection contributed $584 million (4.3% of revenues) and $750 million (5.5% of reveneus), respectively.
KLA's two main product lines are defect inspection and metrology. Its defect inspection tools have broad applications in chip, wafer, reticle, storage, compound semiconductor and MEMS manufacturing. Metrology tools gather critical dimension measurements and assess process dimensions such as film thickness, lithography overlay and surface profiling. These products are used in chip, wafer, reticle and solar device manufacturing. KLA also offers products and services.
In addition to new tools, KLA offers refurbished systems that upgrade equipment and improve yields under the KT-Certified program. These tools are sold to IC, reticle, substrate, MEMS and data storage manufacturers.
Although KLA is a major player in each of its served markets, it faces competition from other large equipment suppliers such as Applied Materials and Hitachi High-Tech Corporation.

A backlog above $12 billion and improving supply availability provide visibility into 2027, while advanced packaging offers added share gains as front-end tools move into packaging flows. Semiconductor Equipment Stocks Slide as Investors Take Profits on a Huge Year: Applied Materials Sinks 7%, Lam Research and KLA Drop 4%
Profit-taking is hammering chipmaking equipment stocks far harder than the broader semiconductor sector, and the gap points to something more specific than a routine pullback after a big year.
Published October 13, 2026, 12:53pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

Semiconductor equipment stocks are giving back ground after a strong year powered by artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT | AMAT Price Prediction) stock is at $461.91, down 7% in afternoon trading, a pullback that still leaves it up 80% year to date. Selling is greatest among the companies that build chipmaking tools, a narrow corner of the chip trade.
Meanwhile, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) stock is trading at $297.04, down 4%, a smaller decline than the one hitting Applied Materials stock. Likewise, KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) shares are slipping 4% to $182.44, keeping pace with Lam Research stock.
Chip stocks as a group are holding up far better. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is down 1%. Over in large-cap tech, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.5%, a much softer reading than anything in the equipment group.
Applied Materials Gives Back Gains After EPIC Center Debut
Applied Materials stock is giving back part of a large advance, with the decline running alongside its equipment peers. One session earlier, the company unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center, known as the EPIC Center, at its Sunnyvale campus. Management describes the site as the world’s largest facility for collaborative semiconductor process and equipment research. Applied Materials expects capital spending there to scale to approximately $5 billion as customer projects begin.
A leading chipmaker joined the center as a founding partner, giving the project a strong start. Recent results also support the longer-term story. In August, Applied Materials reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $3.50 against a $3.39 estimate and guided Q4 FY2026 revenue to about $10.25 billion.
Equipment Makers Slide Harder Than the Broader Chip Group
All three equipment names carry large gains into the pullback, with Lam Research stock up 74% year to date and KLA stock up 51%. Each is falling several times harder than the semiconductor fund that holds them, a split that points at fabrication spending intentions, because the iShares fund also owns chip designers and foundries and its decline serves as broad sector context.
The EPIC Center commits capital to exactly the advanced-node and packaging work that AI buildouts require, and it ties major customers to Applied Materials earlier in the design cycle. In Q3 FY2026, U.S. customers accounted for 15% of Applied Materials’ revenue, while China fell to 28% from 35%. Looking further out, Applied Materials’ chief executive stated in the August results release, “Based on the increased demand visibility we are receiving from our customers, we expect another strong growth year for Applied Materials in 2027.”
Yet, equipment orders are discretionary, and a stock carrying a year-to-date gain of that size has a long way to fall whenever that spending is questioned. Policy adds another layer of risk, since China still made up a large share of Applied Materials’ revenue last quarter. Even after the pullback, Applied Materials shares hold most of their gain for the year, which leaves room for further profit-taking if spending plans shift.
Investors should track whether customer projects at the EPIC Center begin on schedule, since that work supports the bull case. A widening gap between the equipment trio and the iShares fund could signal deeper worries about fabrication budgets, while a narrowing gap could suggest the selling is fading.
Trading in Lam Research stock and KLA stock offers a useful cross-check, since both companies sell into the same fabrication budgets. Investors should keep their positions sized to that kind of volatility.

KLAC Surges 64.5% in a Year: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:26 AM CDT 5 min read
KLA KLAC shares have surged 64.5% over the past year, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector increase of 25.6% and the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry rise of 32.5%.
The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, which include ASML Holding ASML, Advanced Energy AEIS and Entegris ENTG. All three companies are expanding their footprint in the semiconductor industry. ASML Holding, Advanced Energy and Entegris shares have soared 63.4%, 37.3% and 61.8%, respectively, over the past year.
The outperformance can be attributed to strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging. These factors are helping KLAC fend off its competitors such as ASML Holding, Advanced Energy and Entegris.
KLAC Benefits From Strong Semiconductor Demand
KLAC is benefiting from accelerating investments in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, driven by rising AI computing requirements, growing adoption of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and increasing complexity in leading-edge chip manufacturing. The company's strong position in semiconductor process control, wafer inspection and metrology solutions has been a major growth driver.
In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Semiconductor Process Control revenues rose 13% to $3.26 billion, accounting for approximately 89% of total revenues. The segment benefited from continued investments in leading-edge manufacturing and increasing process control intensity across advanced semiconductor technologies.
AI infrastructure remains a major growth catalyst. Increasing AI compute requirements, hyperscale data-center investments, HBM adoption and sophisticated packaging architectures require tighter process control to improve yields and accelerate production ramps. KLA highlighted that customer demand signals have strengthened materially, while visibility continues to improve. The company expects business momentum to accelerate through the second half of 2026 and significant growth to continue in 2027.
Advanced packaging provides another significant growth opportunity. KLA now expects advanced packaging process-control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year and exceeding its previous expectation of high-50% growth. Meanwhile, Specialty Process, PCB and Component Inspection businesses are expected to grow more than 25% in calendar year 2026, supported by high-performance computing and greater package complexity.
The broader semiconductor equipment environment also remains favorable. KLA raised its calendar year 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market estimate, including advanced packaging, to the low-$150-billion range from its previous expectation of more than $140 billion. Broad-based investment across leading-edge logic, foundry, DRAM, HBM, NAND and advanced packaging is expected to sustain capacity expansion. KLA expects second-half 2026 revenues to increase roughly 20% from the first half.
KLAC's Expanding Backlog Strengthens Growth Prospects
KLAC is benefiting from a rapidly expanding backlog, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments and robust demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
KLA's backlog stood at about $12.6 billion, up roughly 60% from fiscal 2025, while the company said the order funnel remains strong. Customer shipment visibility extends through 2027 and, in some cases, into early 2028. Orders generally cover a 12–18-month delivery window, giving investors better visibility into future revenue despite the industry's cyclicality.
KLAC's strong exposure to AI-driven semiconductor investments is expected to benefit the company's top-line growth.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, KLA expects revenues of $4 billion (plus or minus $200 million). Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be $1.16 per share (plus or minus 10 cents). Foundry/logic is expected to account for about 73% of Semiconductor Process Control systems revenues to semiconductor customers, with memory at roughly 27%. Within memory, DRAM is projected to be about 90% and NAND at 10%. Non-GAAP operating expenses are anticipated to be approximately $690 million.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings is pegged at $1.18 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This indicates 34.09% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

Wall Street Analysts See a 27.86% Upside in KLA (KLAC): Can the Stock Really Move This High?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:55 AM CDT 4 min read
Shares of KLA (KLAC) have gained 9.5% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $184, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $235.26 indicates a potential upside of 27.9%.
The mean estimate comprises 27 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $38.15. While the lowest estimate of $170.00 indicates a 7.6% decline from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 76.6% to reach $325.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.
However, an impressive consensus price target is not the only factor that indicates a potential upside in KLAC. This view is strengthened by the agreement among analysts that the company will report better earnings than what they estimated earlier. Though a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't give any idea as to how much the stock could surge, it has proven effective in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for KLAC
Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0.4% over the past month, as one estimate has gone higher compared to no negative revision.
Moreover, KLAC currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much KLAC could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

One Reason KLA Stock Looks Better Than Its Price
Most investors still view KLA (KLAC) as a traditional wafer inspection company. However, the business selling inspection tools for advanced packaging is beginning to stand out, and management ties this demand to the expansion of AI. Packaging may be part of what buyers are currently paying for. The stock costs 51.4 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500, yet overall sales grew 15% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026. A price that high beside that growth rate presents a clear contradiction. So, how big has KLA's packaging business become?
KLA's Packaging Forecast: About $1.1 Billion In Calendar 2026
Management expects about $1.1 billion of revenue from packaging process control systems in calendar 2026. That figure represents an increase of more than 70% from a year earlier. The company provided this raised forecast during its fiscal Q4 2026 call on July 28, 2026, stepping up from an earlier expectation of growth in the high 50% range.
Management stated that the expansion of AI requires new, complex packaging steps, alongside additional KLA systems to bring those processes to high-volume production. Furthermore, customers adopting newer packaging methods such as hybrid bonding are buying more inspection tools, the company said.
Packaging remains a small fraction of the overall business at KLA, which recorded $13.6 billion in sales over the last twelve months. Yet management expects this segment to grow more than 70% in calendar 2026.
Does Packaging Help KLA With Rising Costs?
Not directly. While packaging brings KLA more sales, the segment does not alter what the company pays for parts.
Costs surfaced repeatedly on the July 28 call. KLA is buying memory components at higher prices, and management indicated those headwinds will "likely continue through next year." When asked why the company could not simply raise its own prices to match, executives explained that it is difficult to adjust pricing on existing orders. Instead, new prices are established when new products come out.
Despite these material costs, gross margin reached 62.4% in fiscal Q4 2026, landing at the upper end of KLA's guidance. Looking ahead to the September quarter, which KLA has yet to report, management forecast 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point.
Sales are also expanding. Management listed advanced packaging among the factors behind its record fiscal Q4 revenue of $3.66 billion. The company then guided to $4 billion for the September quarter, plus or minus $200 million.
Can KLA Build Its Tools Fast Enough?
Not during the first half of calendar 2026. Management noted that shortages of some long-lead-time materials held the company back during that period. KLA's lead times currently sit at about 12 months across the company, stretching closer to 18 to 24 months on certain products. Building new capacity for those components can take 12 to 24 months. KLA says it is adding capacity to support the demand it expects.
That timeline matters for the packaging business because the cited revenue figure is a forecast for the year, not a recorded result. KLA must physically build the tools before it can sell them.
Ultimately, KLA's packaging revenue forecast for calendar 2026 is the number to watch when the company reports its September quarter.

Now you know KLAC better. And that's our purpose: to make you informed before you invest your money. However, making a bet on a single stock carries its own risks.
